VERDICT ON THE METER FIRST: yes, anchoring the subscription to jobs live at once works, and it is the right call over turnover — it is what ServiceM8 already sells (by jobs, unlimited users), it does not punish adding site staff, and it scales from a sole trader to a 20-person firm. But a flat count of jobs cannot honestly price a 15-job firm, because it cannot tell a £2m firm running 15 extensions from a £600k firm running 15 kitchens: both land at £179. Weight the jobs by size, add capped overage, and the same headline gets the £2m firm to £251–£349 a month, which is as far as a jobs meter can honestly go. Beyond that the value has to come from the fee categories and from add-ons that charge for something observable, never from a counterfactual.

RECOMMENDED LADDER (ex VAT, per business, unlimited users, quoting free forever, identical 10% success fee on every tier):
- Solo — £29/month, £290/year: 3 places live at once, plus up to 10 micro-jobs under £1,000 at no charge.
- Builder (the hero plan) — £69/month, £690/year: 10 places, plus micro-jobs.
- Firm — £179/month, £1,790/year: 20 places, plus micro-jobs, plus (when built) Construction Act payment and pay-less notices, retention tracking, multi-approver sign-off, office dashboard, evidence-pack export, priority support.
- Contractor — £349/month, £3,490/year: 40 places, plus everything in Firm, multi-entity.
- Custom above 40 places.
- Places: a live job takes 1 place up to £25,000 accepted net value, 2 places over £25,000 to £100,000, 3 places over £100,000 (greater of accepted and quoted, frozen at switch-live).
- Overage rule: £9 per extra place per month on every tier, checked only at switch-live (upgrade / add on overage / leave accepted-but-not-live), derived from the month's peak concurrent places, stopping automatically when the peak falls back inside the tier, and capped so subscription plus overage never exceeds the next tier's price. After two consecutive months of overage at or above the step-up difference, prompt an upgrade; never auto-upgrade.
- Counting rules in one breath: counts from switch-live to lock, close or 60-day dormancy pause (45-day prompt); paused jobs accept no commercial records and resume on any; post-lock never re-counts and new work is a new linked job; same customer + same site + contiguous dates = one job on combined value; once-only upward re-band on approved variations; imports count from day 31; first live job free for up to 90 days with the success fee applying normally; monthly plans step down any month; annual plans fix places and use overage; every bill names the jobs that counted and why; places and overage are one tenant-level subscription under D09 v3, never a per-job base fee, cap or credit, and never offset against the success fee.

REVENUE BY ARCHETYPE (assumptions stated: Solo 19 jobs/year all ≤£25k, 3 live; Small firm 24 jobs/year, 6 live as 3 × 1-place + 3 × 2-place = 9 places; Firm 33 jobs/year, 15 live as 4 × 1 + 9 × 2 + 2 × 3 = 28 places; the founder's candidate ladder assumed to have limits of 3 / 8 / 20 / 40 live jobs since none were stated):
- Solo: £29 → £348/year (£18 per job, 0.23% of turnover). Same under the founder's candidate.
- Small firm: £69 → £828/year (£34.50 per job, 0.14%). Same under the founder's candidate.
- Firm: £179 + 8 × £9 = £251 → £3,012/year (£91 per job, 0.15%), or £349 → £4,188 on a flat Contractor plan (0.21%). The founder's flat candidate earns £2,148 from the same firm. The lift is 40–95%, and the firm still pays about half of 15 Tradify Plus seats (£7,920).
- Success fee on top, everywhere, illustrative only because no UK data exists on unbilled extras (research report, confidence table): if 20% of jobs yield a qualifying catch worth 3% of job value, roughly £90 / £360 / £1,190 a year, before any cash supplier refunds or withheld-payment cases.

HONEST ANSWER ON THE 15-JOB FIRM: a flat jobs meter cannot capture enough — it leaves the £2m firm at £179 (0.11% of turnover), six times the sole trader's price for thirteen times the turnover and seven times the job size, and it cannot separate that firm from a much smaller one with the same job count. The weighted meter reaches £251–£349, roughly 0.15–0.21% of turnover. If prevention is worth about 1% of turnover (an assumption, in line with Buildbite's self-reported 30% change-order lift but unproven), the subscription captures about 15–20% of it and the builder keeps the rest, which is the honest shape of a watchdog product and the story the pricing page should tell. A jobs meter will not go past £349 for a 15-job firm without becoming a turnover meter in disguise; do not try.

OTHER WAYS TO CAPTURE VALUE, RANKED BY CREDIBILITY (all need their own decision record; none touches the fee rules or the shadow bill):
1. Weighted places (above) — the largest honest lever; already covered by frozen data.
2. Tier-gated workflow depth for Firm/Contractor (notices, retention, multi-approver, dashboards, packs, priority support) — gate workflow, never a detection; every tier keeps every check so the fee base and the trust story survive.
3. Capped overage and annual two-months-free — capture seasonal peaks and cash.
4. Hosted-payments platform margin of about 0.3% on customer payments through the M4 Stripe/GoCardless hosted surfaces (JobGuard never holds funds; processor rate passed through) — roughly £180 / £450 / £600 a year on assumed shares; standard for the category (Fergus 1.6% + 20p).
5. Withheld-payment recovery cases — already a 10% category; make case-opening prominent because late payment is the one well-measured pain (£26bn owed, 14,000 closures a year), and automate Late Payment Act interest and fixed compensation for B2B customers at Firm+ (the builder keeps the statutory sums; the 10% applies to principal only).
6. Evidence-pack assembly for disputes: £49 per pack on Solo/Builder, included on Firm+, raw export always free; the packs already exist (M4-3-S, #92).
7. Onboarding/import service, £199–£499 one-off for Firm/Contractor migrations (Payaca charges £1,500; Buildertrend $500–2,000).
8. Accountant/bookkeeper practice plan later (per-client pricing, Dext-style).
9. A monthly 'flagged before you paid' statement as the retention and upgrade lever, worded as 'flagged for your decision' — §14.1 forbids 'JobGuard saved you £X' before settled cash.
10. Pilot-measure only: a D03 v3 candidate charging a small flat amount per documented pre-payment supplier correction over £100. The supplier's corrected invoice makes the counterfactual stronger than generic prevention, but it charges on prevented spend, which today earns nothing, and builders may just stop recording corrections. Do not ship without measurement and a fairness check.
Named and rejected on trust: merchant/supplier commissions or preferred-supplier placement (compromises the invoice watchdog); selling builders' data or their customers as leads (D12 and word-of-mouth risk); a homeowner-side bill checker (paid by both sides of one invoice). Insurance or invoice-finance referrals are a milder conflict: full disclosure or leave them out.

NEXT STEPS: draft D09 v3 with the bands, thresholds, overage price and ceiling; add the metering events and D11 advisory signals to the build plan under 'Discovered later'; in the no-charge pilot measure the accepted-value distribution per archetype, jobs live at once by month, dormancy and pause behaviour, and recovered money per job so the £25k/£100k lines, the 90-day trial and the fee assumptions are replaced by data before anyone is charged; run the £29-versus-£39 Solo test and card-at-switch-live test the research recommends. This is analysis for those decisions, not approval of them.

result.live_job_definition:
A live job is a JobGuard job in the `live` state of the §3.1 job spine (draft → quoting → accepted → live → invoiced → paid): it starts at the server-committed `switch_live` command that freezes the baseline (M1-7) and ends at the earliest of (a) the server-committed `final_account_lock` (§14.4), (b) an explicit post-activation closure/cancellation command (§3.1), or (c) dormancy (60 consecutive days with no metered activity). It is a capacity unit, not a value unit: one job = one tenant + one accepting customer party + one site address + one accepted quote baseline (`baseline_quote_version_id`). A second accepted quote is a second job.

Edge cases:
- Quoting states (draft, quoting, accepted, lost) never count: free quoting never bills (AGENTS §5.10). A won-but-not-live job is not live; it is only a D11 advisory signal.
- Snagging before lock counts (the builder is still on site capturing proof). Snagging after lock: the job is no longer live, but a calendar day with metered activity (proof upload, PO, supplier document, variation logged, diary/voice note, customer message, final-account revision, invoice issue) counts that job for that day only (pence, not pounds).
- Retention periods: a locked/invoiced job with a retention balance outstanding is not live. Retention due dates, releases and any later recovery case are payment-side facts and never re-enter the meter.
- Paused jobs: an explicit `PauseJob` command (customer delay, weather, materials, planning) stops counting from the next calendar day; any metered activity un-pauses the job and it counts that day. D13 must-surface and safety findings still fire on a paused job.
- Jobs that never lock: after 60 consecutive days without metered activity the job becomes `dormant`, stops counting from the next period and the builder is prompted to finish it; activity revives it. Invoice/payment activity with no lock remains a D11 advisory signal (§14.4). Forgetting to lock never costs the builder money; it costs them the final check.
- Imported in-flight jobs (`adopt-job.v1`): `lifecyclePoint: live` counts from the import commit, using the builder-attested accepted net value for the small-job test; `lifecyclePoint: invoiced` never counts (payment tracking and recovery only).
- Trial and pilot jobs: a business's first switch-live starts the trial; that one job is excluded from the meter until it locks or for 90 days, whichever is first (research report §"Let the trial run until the first job is live"); the success fee applies normally on it. `pilot_no_charge` jobs are excluded by the explicit D09 inclusion rule (M4-14), never by default.
- Small jobs (recommended option 4a): accepted net value under £2,000 ex VAT at switch-live takes no slot (fair use: 10 at once); if approved variations lift the net value above £4,000 it takes a slot from that day, shown on the job.

Every boundary is a server timestamp on an immutable event (switch-live, lock, closure, pause/unpause, dormancy, import), so the meter is replayable from the audit chain and a cached counter can never trigger a charge (M4-14; AGENTS §5.4).
counting_rules: Unit is job-days. For each calendar day D (Europe/London) in the billing period, live(D) = the number of the tenant's jobs in metered state at any instant of D (live, unlocked, not paused, not dormant, not trial/pilot-exempt, not a fair-use small job) plus any job outside metered state that has metered activity recorded on D. Boundaries use server commit timestamps only; client or offline capture times never move a boundary (AGENTS §5.12).
Each tier includes S slots. over(D) = max(0, live(D) − S). Overage job-days for the period = Σ over(D).

Overage charge = roundHalfEven(overage_job_days × £20.00 × 100 ÷ days_in_period) pence, computed once per period as an exact rational with a single rounding (AGENTS §5.5). £20 per extra job-month ≈ 66p per job-day in a 30-day month, so a one-day overlap between an ending and a starting job costs pence and no grace period is needed.

Auto-overage ceiling in jobs per tier: Solo 2, Builder 5, Firm 8, Contractor 16. Up to the ceiling, extra jobs run automatically under the D05 bounded standing authority whose monetary ceiling is plan price + ceiling × £20 (Solo £69, Builder £169, Firm £339, Contractor £669). Ceilings are chosen so the next plan is never dearer than continuing on overage.

At the ceiling, switching a further job live requires a one-tap upgrade Decision showing the exact new price and the pro-rata amount for the rest of the period (AGENTS §5.3: the button creates and approves the Decision; M4-14: an over-limit event raises the required Decision). Already-live jobs are never blocked, throttled or hidden; only the next switch-live waits for the tap. A worker cannot upgrade a tenant.
Tier fit uses the instantaneous live count at the moment of switch-live; overage money uses job-days. Both derive from the same immutable event log and must reconcile in the M4-14 fixtures.
Downgrades take effect at the next period boundary and only if the current live count is within the new plan's slots + ceiling. No mid-period tier change except a builder-approved upgrade.

Late or replayed events (offline sync, replays, reopen) re-derive the affected period and post a linked compensating subscription line in the next period; posted period lines are never edited (AGENTS §5.5, §5.7).

Pause: `PauseJob` stops counting from the next calendar day; any metered activity un-pauses the job and it counts that day. Dormant: 60 consecutive days with no metered activity; stops counting from the next period; revived by activity.

Metered activity (re-counts a post-lock, paused or dormant job for that day): purchase order created/changed; supplier invoice, delivery note or credit received; proof or progress photo uploaded; variation logged, priced or approved; diary or voice note; customer message sent or received through JobGuard; final-account revision; invoice issue. Not metered: recording a customer payment or retention release, reveal dispositions, viewing or exporting, fee statements, D11 signal review, evidence-pack generation.

Small-job allowance: accepted net value under £2,000 ex VAT at switch-live (attested value for imports) takes no slot, fair use 10 concurrent; above £4,000 net after approved variations it takes a slot from that day. Three or more sub-£2,000 jobs for the same customer party and site within 90 days count as one job for the allowance (deterministic, shown on the job, and a D11 advisory signal).

Trial: the business's first switch-live starts the trial; that job is excluded until it locks or 90 days, whichever first; the 10% fee applies normally on it. Pilot jobs follow the explicit D09 inclusion rule; exemption is never a default.
Annual plans: plan price prepaid at 'two months free'; overage is billed monthly in arrears at the same £20, never discounted; the auto-overage ceiling is unchanged.

Subscription pause (not a job pause): a monthly plan with zero live jobs for a whole billing period may pause at £0 for up to 3 periods in any 12; quoting stays free while paused; switching any job live ends the pause. Untested (research seasonality note); put it in D09 v3 as a pilot experiment, not a promise.
Display: the job list always shows 'N of S slots in use; next slot £20/month (or free until [date])', rebuilt from events, not a cached counter, so the meter is never a surprise.

Definition of a job for counting: one accepted quote, one accepting customer party, one site address. Multiple phases of one customer's project under one accepted quote are one job; separate accepted quotes are separate jobs; two customer parties can never share a job because acceptance and invoicing bind one party.

options.name: Option 1 — Pure per-live-job price with a monthly minimum
options.structure: £12 per live job per month (job-days, pro rata), minimum £29/month (covers ~2.4 jobs). Unlimited users, no tiers. Optional volume steps (£12 for jobs 1–10, £10 for 11–25, £8 above) if a volume discount is wanted.
options.per_job_economics: Constant £12/job-month (40p/job-day). Lifetime subscription cost per job at the archetype durations (1.6 / 2.75 / 5.4 months): Solo ~£19, Small ~£33, Firm ~£65; 0.24% / 0.13% / 0.11% of turnover.

revenue_by_archetype.solo: £30/month at 2.5 live jobs → £360/yr (at 2 jobs the £29 minimum applies)
revenue_by_archetype.small_firm: £66/month at 5.5 live jobs → £792/yr
revenue_by_archetype.firm: £180/month at 15 live jobs → £2,160/yr

options.pros: Fairest, simplest meter: bill = usage; no cliffs, no tier gaming, no upgrade Decisions; a firm automatically pays 6× a solo; explained in one sentence ('£12 a job a month, minimum £29').
options.cons: Taxi-meter aversion and flat-rate bias (Prelec & Loewenstein 1998; Lambrecht & Skiera 2006, in the research notes): builders prefer a predictable flat number. A variable bill needs a D05 standing authority with a hard monetary ceiling, which pure per-job lacks unless you add one (and then you have tiers again). No hero middle plan for the compromise effect. Per-job price cannot rise with firm size without a rate card. Undercharges firms against the per-user comparator (£480–£555/month on Tradify or Powered Now for 15 staff).

options.name: Option 2 — Tiers by live jobs with forced upgrade at the limit (founder's ladder shape)
options.structure: Flat plan per business with a hard slot limit; switching a job live beyond the limit requires an upgrade Decision first (M4-14 'enforces the agreed limit'). Founder's ladder: £29 ≤3 / £69 ≤5 / £179 ≤10 / £349 ≤20 / custom above 20.
options.per_job_economics: Per slot at the limit: £9.67 / £13.80 / £17.90 / £17.45. Below the limit the marginal job is free; the job that crosses it costs the whole gap: the 6th job costs £110/month, the 11th £170/month.

revenue_by_archetype.small_firm: £69 at 5 live, £179 at 6 live → £828 or £2,148/yr; the archetype sits exactly on the cliff
revenue_by_archetype.firm: £349 (15 live on the 20-slot tier) → £4,188/yr; ≈£126 per job; 0.21% of turnover

options.pros: One number per tier; flat and predictable (flat-rate bias works for you); simplest D05 mandate (fixed renewals); highest firm revenue of the honest options; matches how the market prices (ServiceM8 steps).
options.cons: Cliffs drive gaming exactly where the archetypes sit (5→6 jobs = 2.6× the price). Forced upgrade at the moment of switch-live is the worst possible friction: the builder is on site with a won job. The research report (§'Charge for live jobs, not people') explicitly advises suggesting an upgrade rather than blocking. Gaps of 2.6× and 1.95× make each upgrade feel like a penalty, not a purchase.

options.name: Option 3 — Tiers plus per-job overage instead of forced upgrades (recommended shape)
options.structure: Solo £29 (3 slots) / Builder £69 (6) / Firm £179 (12) / Contractor £349 (24) / custom above 40 live jobs. £20 per extra job-month pro rata by job-days, automatic up to a per-tier ceiling of 2 / 5 / 8 / 16 extra jobs; at the ceiling the next switch-live is a one-tap upgrade, never a block. Ceilings are set so plan + overage ≤ next plan (Solo+2 = £69 = Builder; Builder+5 = £169 < £179; Firm+8 = £339 < £349).

revenue_by_archetype.solo: £29 → £348/yr (2.5 avg; a month peaking at 4 jobs costs £49)
revenue_by_archetype.small_firm: £69 → £828/yr (5.5 avg within 6 slots; a 7th job for a fortnight ≈ +£9)
revenue_by_archetype.firm: £239 → £2,868/yr on Firm + 3 extra jobs (15 avg); £349 Contractor if they run 21+

options.pros: No cliffs, so no reason to keep the 6th job off. Flat-rate feel with a bounded variable part, which is what D05 'bounded standing authority' needs. The upgrade tap is always the cheaper choice at the ceiling, so it never feels punitive. Three real plans with a hero in the middle. Per-slot price rises mildly with tier (bigger firms' jobs are bigger, carry more documents and more value) — the founder's own ladder shape without its cliffs.
options.cons: Two numbers to explain (plan and £20 extra). Overage needs M4-14 metering, a D05 ceiling and per-period exact arithmetic before any charging (currently optional in the plan; becomes mandatory). Firm revenue (£239) is below the founder's £349 unless option 4b is adopted. A builder can sit at a ceiling indefinitely (Builder + 5 = £169) instead of upgrading — acceptable, since it is only £10 short of Firm.

options.name: Option 4a — Option 3 plus a small-job allowance (jobs under £2,000 free)
options.structure: As option 3. Jobs with accepted net value under £2,000 at switch-live take no slot (fair use 10 at once); above £4,000 after approved variations a job takes a slot from that day; three or more sub-£2k jobs for the same customer party and site within 90 days count as one.
options.per_job_economics: Same tier and overage prices. Small jobs cost £0 subscription; JobGuard's processing cost on them is low (few documents) and quoting on them was free anyway. Assumed share of live jobs under £2k: Solo 30%, Small 15%, Firm 5% (assumption).

revenue_by_archetype.solo: £29 → £348/yr (countable ≈1.75 of 2.5; unchanged, and a 4-job month becomes free instead of £49)
revenue_by_archetype.small_firm: £69 → £828/yr (countable ≈4.7; unchanged)
revenue_by_archetype.firm: £224 → £2,688/yr (countable ≈14.25 → 2.25 extra jobs; about £180/yr less than option 3)

options.pros: Removes the 'keep small jobs off JobGuard' vector where it bites hardest (solos doing repairs and day-jobs). Brings evidence and habit onto the platform at near-zero cost. Costs almost nothing on the archetypes (only over-limit firms lose ~£15/month). Easy to say: 'Small jobs under £2k don't count'.
options.cons: New gaming vector: splitting work into sub-£2k quotes (mitigated by the same-customer-site rule and the fair-use cap). One more rule on the pricing page. The £2,000 threshold and the £4,000 trip-point are load-bearing numbers that must go into D09 v3.

options.name: Option 4b — Option 3/4a plus a big-job slot weighting (OPTIONAL DEVIATION from the pure jobs meter)
options.structure: A job whose accepted net value at switch-live is above £50,000 occupies 2 slots (above £150,000: 3). Everything else as 4a. Labelled deviation: it re-introduces contract value into the meter, which the founder rejected as the primary meter; here it is a secondary weight, not the unit.
options.per_job_economics: A £60k job costs £29.84/month on Firm (2 × £14.92) or £40 on overage — still 0.05% of its value per month. Assumed share of jobs over £50k: Solo 0%, Small 5%, Firm 50% (assumption; average firm job £60k).

revenue_by_archetype.solo: £29 → £348/yr (unchanged)
revenue_by_archetype.small_firm: £69 → £828/yr (unchanged; one big job would use 2 of 6 slots)
revenue_by_archetype.firm: £349 Contractor → £4,188/yr (15 jobs ≈ 22.5 slots, above Firm's 12 + 8 ceiling); matches the founder's £349 outcome for firms

options.pros: Closes most of the size disparity (a £60k job pays about 2× an £8k job, not 1×) without a turnover meter. The only option that lifts firm revenue to the founder's £349. Defensible on cost (big jobs carry more POs, deliveries, photos and shadow-bill work) and against the per-user comparator (£480–£555).
options.cons: It is contract-value pricing by the back door. Two thresholds to explain. Incentive to under-attest imported values or to quote big projects as phases (which then become separate jobs and pay anyway). Weakens the research's 'compare on one or two numbers' advice. Should wait for pilot cost data (§14.17 measures subscription revenue against demonstrated value).

options.name: Comparator A — founder's candidate ladder (£29 ≤2–3 / £69 ≤5 / £179 ≤10 / £349 ≤20 / custom), forced upgrades
options.structure: As stated, no overage, custom above 20. 'Up to 2–3' is ambiguous; pick 3.
options.per_job_economics: £9.67 / £13.80 / £17.90 / £17.45 per slot at the limit. The rising per-slot price is right; the 2.6× and 1.95× gaps are the problem.
options.pros: Highest revenue of any honest ladder; rising per-slot reflects value and document volume; one number per tier.
options.cons: The 5→6 cliff lands on the small-firm archetype; the 10→11 cliff (£170) on growing firms; no overage means block-or-upgrade at switch-live; a firm at 11 jobs pays £349 for 20 slots it does not use.

options.name: Comparator B — research report ladder (£29 ≤3 / £59 ≤10 / £119 ≤25 / custom)
options.structure: Three tiers, unlimited users, forced upgrades implied, 'Contractor' on request above 25.
options.per_job_economics: £9.67 / £5.90 / £4.76 per slot: a steep volume discount, the opposite of cost and value.
options.pros: Cheapest and safest against gaming and against Checkatrade's free tools; allowances so generous the meter almost never binds.
options.cons: Leaves most of the firm's value on the table: a 15-staff firm pays £119 against £480–£555 on per-user rivals, and 4× cheaper is not a quality signal. 10 slots for £59 means the small firm never grows into the next tier. Per-slot price falls with size.

gaming.vector: Keeping jobs (especially small ones) off JobGuard to stay in a cheaper tier
gaming.mitigation: Small-job allowance (under £2,000 free); £20 overage instead of a cliff (the 6th job costs £20, not £110); first-live-job trial; job-day metering so a short overlap costs pence; the value the builder forgoes on the job itself (PO price checks, proof gates, the final check); D11 'won but not live' advisory signal. JobGuard loses catch revenue on off-platform jobs, so allowances stay generous (research report §'Charge for live jobs, not people').

gaming.vector: Merging several customers into one job
gaming.mitigation: A job binds one accepting customer party at acceptance (§3.1) and one invoice recipient; two customers cannot both accept one quote or be invoiced from one job; variation customer-approval goes to that party only. Deterministic, not a penalty.

gaming.vector: Merging phases or sites of one customer into one job
gaming.mitigation: Allowed by design: the meter is capacity and one accepted quote = one job; a merged £150k project takes one slot (2–3 under option 4b). The builder pays with a muddier final account and a weaker shadow-bill match. D11 advisory signal: accepted value above 3× the tenant's median with multiple site addresses in evidence.

gaming.vector: One 'job' per site with many customers (a block of flats)
gaming.mitigation: Prohibited by definition: one accepting party per job. A management company or landlord accepting one quote for many units is legitimately one customer and one job.

gaming.vector: Locking or closing early to stop the meter
gaming.mitigation: Lock ends the meter, but any post-lock metered activity re-counts the job for that day. One immutable lock per job, so an early lock only cuts the builder's own final check short (only pre-lock evidence qualifies, §14.6). Cancellation after activation is an audited closure with financial adjustment; activity after closure re-counts and raises a D11 signal.

gaming.vector: Never locking; invoicing outside JobGuard
gaming.mitigation: Dormancy after 60 idle days stops the meter (builder-friendly, so it is not a revenue lever either way). D11 'invoice or payment activity with no lock'. Invoice issue through JobGuard requires the lock, so the builder also forgoes billing and payment tooling. This is the fee-side residual risk already accepted in §14.10, not a subscription leak.

gaming.vector: Pausing jobs on the 1st and un-pausing when needed
gaming.mitigation: Any metered activity un-pauses the job and counts that day; pause is explicit and visible in the job list; the meter is job-days, so a genuinely idle job costs nothing and an active one pays.

gaming.vector: Splitting work into sub-£2,000 quotes to use the allowance
gaming.mitigation: Fair-use cap of 10 small jobs; three or more sub-£2k jobs for the same customer party and site within 90 days count as one for the allowance; a small job that grows past £4,000 net through approved variations takes a slot from that day; D11 advisory signal.

gaming.vector: Under-attesting imported job values (small-job or big-job thresholds)
gaming.mitigation: Imported lineage is already 'builder_attested_weaker' and the attested value also bounds recovery evidence quality on that job; D11 signal when the final-account value exceeds 2× the attested value.

gaming.vector: Trial abuse: a new business per job
gaming.mitigation: One trial per business identity (company number/UTR, phone, payment method); card at first switch-live; trial ends at first lock or 90 days.

gaming.vector: Splitting a firm into several 'businesses' to stay in Solo
gaming.mitigation: D11 advisory signal on shared users, phones and addresses across tenants; terms. Low priority: per-slot prices are close across tiers (£9.67–£14.92), so the gain is small.

gaming.vector: Timing games around the period boundary (downgrade then overage; switch live at 23:59)
gaming.mitigation: Downgrades only at period end and only within the new plan's ceiling; overage is job-days, so a late-night switch-live costs pence; boundaries use server time. All mitigations are deterministic rules or D11 advisory signals; none changes a price or takes an account action outside a valid standing authorization.

result.size_disparity_fix:
The disparity is real and should be named rather than hidden: a £60k job on Firm costs £14.92/month, an £8k job on Solo £9.67, so the meter charges firms 0.14% of turnover and solos 0.23%. Six levers, in the order to pull them:
1. Accept it structurally. The subscription is a capacity charge; the 10% success fee is the value charge and already scales with job size (a missed £2,400 extra on a £60k job pays £240; the same 4% miss on an £8k job pays £32). Retention money and withheld payments are also proportionally bigger on big jobs.
2. Let the per-slot price rise mildly with tier (£9.67 → £11.50 → £14.92), the founder's own ladder shape, justified by document volume and value and invisible on the page (one number per tier).
3. Small-job allowance at the bottom (option 4a) so a solo is not paying £9.67 for a £900 repair.
4. Put firm-scale features in Firm and Contractor: interim applications and staged invoicing (M4-18), retention tracking and release chasing, subcontractor POs, accounting-connector sync, evidence packs on demand. Two or three features, not a grid.
5. Big-job slot weighting (option 4b, labelled deviation): adopt only if pilot cost data (§14.17) shows firm jobs cost more than 2× to process, or firm-tier revenue lands well under the per-user comparator; it lifts the firm archetype from £239 to £349.
6. Do not fix it with turnover or contract value as the meter: rejected, and it would push the subscription toward a second percentage fee alongside the 10%.
result.recommendation:
VERDICT ON THE METER. Yes, live jobs works, with three conditions. It is a capacity meter the builder controls and understands, it produces a 12× spread (£29 → £349+) between a solo and a 20-job firm, and it lands under the per-user comparator at every point (£29 vs Tradify £34 for one user; £69 vs £170–£220 for five; £239 vs £480–£555 for fifteen). Cross-check, not a re-argument: it yields 0.14–0.23% of turnover, i.e. the same band as the rejected turnover meter, but measured by something visible and fair. The conditions: (1) it needs an overage, because cliffs put the gaming incentive exactly where the archetypes sit; (2) it needs a precise definition of 'live' (above) or snagging, retention and forgotten jobs will make it feel like a tax; (3) it caps out around £350–£700/month even for the largest target firm, so anything beyond that must come from the success fee and the levers below, not the subscription.

RECOMMENDED LADDER (all ex VAT, per business, unlimited users, quoting free forever, 10% success fee identical on every plan):
- Solo £29/month (£290/yr): 3 live jobs. £9.67 per slot.
- Builder £69/month (£690/yr), the hero plan: 6 live jobs. £11.50 per slot.
- Firm £179/month (£1,790/yr): 12 live jobs. £14.92 per slot.
- Contractor £349/month (£3,490/yr): 24 live jobs. £14.54 per slot. Above 40 live jobs: priced on request.
- Extra jobs: £20 per job per month, pro rata by the day (about 66p a day), automatic up to 2 / 5 / 8 / 16 extra jobs; at that ceiling the next switch-live is a one-tap move to the next plan, which is never dearer than continuing on overage. Existing jobs are never blocked.
- Small jobs under £2,000 accepted net value do not take a slot (fair use 10 at once; a small job that grows past £4,000 through approved variations takes a slot from that day).
- Trial: the first job a business switches live is free until it locks or 90 days, card taken at that switch-live, success fee applies normally. Annual at 'two months free' on the plan only; overage never discounted. Monthly plans may pause at £0 for up to 3 months in 12 when no job is live (pilot experiment).
- Counting: job-days per billing period; live from switch-live to lock, closure or 60-day dormancy; explicit pause; post-lock activity counts that day only; imported jobs count from import if 'live', never if 'invoiced'; server timestamps only; exact rational arithmetic with one half-even rounding per period; upgrades by Decision, never by a worker (M4-14, D05).

What a job costs per month at each tier: Solo £9.67, Builder £11.50, Firm £14.92, Contractor £14.54, extra job £20. Effective price by live-job count: 3→£29, 4→£49, 5→£69, 6→£69, 8→£109, 10→£149, 12→£179, 15→£239, 20→£339, 24→£349, 30→£469, 40→£669. Lifetime subscription cost per job at archetype durations: Solo ~£18, Small ~£35, Firm ~£86.

REVENUE BY ARCHETYPE (assumptions: Solo 2.5 live jobs avg, 19 jobs/yr at £8k, 1.6 months each; Small firm 5.5 live, 24 jobs/yr at £25k, 2.75 months; Firm 15 live, 33 jobs/yr at £60k, 5.4 months; overage on average concurrency, peaks slightly higher):
- Solo: £29 → £348/yr. Founder's ladder £348. Research ladder £348.
- Small firm: £69 → £828/yr. Founder's ladder £828 at 5 jobs but £2,148 at 6 (the cliff). Research £708.
- Firm: £239 → £2,868/yr (Firm + 3 extra); £349 → £4,188 if 4b big-job weighting is adopted or they run 21+. Founder's ladder £4,188. Research £1,428.
Illustrative mix of 1,000 paying builders (60/30/10): ≈£744k/yr subscription, ≈£62/month ARPA, before any success fee.

Against the founder's ladder: same Solo price; same £69 at five jobs; removes the 5→6 and 10→11 cliffs; keeps the rising per-slot shape; costs about £110/month per firm archetype unless 4b is adopted. Against the research ladder: same Solo; £10 more for the small firm in exchange for slots it actually needs; roughly double for firms, which the per-user comparator supports.

HOW ELSE TO CAPTURE THE VALUE (prevention is the bulk of it and cannot honestly carry a fee; these are the credible levers, each with its trust flag):
1. Pre-payment supplier corrections as a new D03 category (strongest untapped lever). Today prevented spend earns nothing. The narrow, provable case is: JobGuard flags a supplier line above the PO/agreed price; the supplier issues a credit note or revised invoice referencing that invoice before payment. No counterfactual is needed: the supplier's own corrected document proves the overcharge existed and was corrected after the flag. A lower rate (e.g. 5% of the documented reduction, capped per invoice) charged only when the corrected document is on file. Needs D03 v3 and a D01 revision; not a re-argument, a flagged future decision. Trust risk: low-moderate ('I'd have spotted it'); mitigated by the rate and by showing the three-way-match work (Buell & Norton labour illusion, research §'The hidden final check').
2. Retention money. Commercial jobs hold 3–5% retention and much of it is never claimed. Track retention due dates, prompt the release request, and if withheld beyond the D03 threshold the builder can open a recovery case: 10% under the existing `withheld_customer_payment` category. No new policy beyond the threshold. Firm-tier value.
3. Statutory late-payment interest and compensation (B2B customers only: 8% + base and the £40/£70/£100 fixed sums). JobGuard computes and adds them to reminders; interest recovered inside a recovery case is new money. Extending 'net principal' to recovered statutory interest needs a D03 revision. Consumer customers excluded (Late Payment Act is B2B only, research §'No rival sells…').
4. Payment-rail margin at M4: hosted Stripe/GoCardless surfaces with a small platform fee to the builder on top of provider fees (e.g. +0.3% card, +20p Direct Debit), like Fergus's 1.6% + 20p. Never holds funds (direct charges to the builder's account). Rough size: Solo ~£135/yr, Firm ~£1,200/yr. Trust risk low; must be disclosed; the builder cannot surcharge consumers.
5. Firm-scale packaging without value metering: interim applications/staged invoicing (M4-18), retention tracking, evidence packs on demand, accounting-connector sync, subcontractor POs in Firm/Contractor.
6. Evidence or dispute pack as a paid one-off (e.g. £49–£149 per pack, included on Firm+) when a dispute or adjudication arises: low volume, high willingness to pay.
7. A monthly 'value receipt' (VALUE-2): 'caught before you paid £X; proof captured on N items; extras tracked £Y'. Not a charge, but the only honest way to make prevention felt so the subscription is renewed and upgraded (Soman & Gourville: bundled subscriptions dull attention).
Ruled out: a paid quote-check add-on (AGENTS §5.10: quoting never bills); a success fee on prevented spend without a supplier document (unprovable counterfactual); merchant referral or rebates (would compromise the invoice watchdog; say so plainly); selling leads or data (trust); insurance or warranty products (regulated). Do not touch the 10% or the no-offset rule.

WHAT THIS NEEDS. This is analysis, not approval: D09 stays `proposed`. To act on it: D09 v3 records the ladder, slots, £20 overage, ceilings, £2,000/£4,000 small-job rule, trial, annual and pause; M4-14 moves from optional to required (job-day aggregation, ceilings, upgrade Decisions, replay fixtures for the effective-price table above); D05 records the overage ceiling as the bounded standing authority; D03 v3 and D01 revisions if levers 1 or 3 are pursued. Before any charging: the 10–20 structured price conversations and the £29-vs-£39 sign-up test the research report asks for, plus pilot measurement of live-job counts, job durations and small-job share per archetype, since every archetype number here is an assumption.

ideas.name: Live-jobs ladder: Solo / Builder / Firm / Contractor (the meter itself)
ideas.mechanism: Tenant subscription metered on peak concurrent live jobs per billing month, derived from immutable switch-live (M1-7) and final-account-lock (SV-4) events; a job is live from switch-live until lock or an explicit close, inactivity never closes it. Tiers per report §Recommendation: Solo ≤3 £29, Builder ≤10 £59, Firm ≤25 £119, Contractor >25 on request; unlimited users; quoting free. Locking frees a slot, which pushes builders toward the event that triggers the final check. Over-limit never blocks switch-live (see I02). Platform invoice prints period, tier, peak count and source events.
ideas.who_pays: Builder business, monthly ex VAT; never per job, never per user
ideas.assumptions: Archetype live counts (2–3 / 5–6 / 15) sit inside allowances; prices are the report's recommendation, not D09 values. Verdict on the meter: it works. It is the ServiceM8 unit builders already accept, tracks workload not turnover, does not penalise site staff who feed evidence, and is auditable from explicit commands. Three honest weaknesses: (1) job-size blind — a firm running three £400k jobs lands on Solo and a £2m firm pays £1,428 where Procore-style volume pricing would take £2–4k, so top-end value must come from the success fee and add-ons (I03/I04 are the job-count-preserving fixes); (2) definition gaming — jobs kept off JobGuard or never switched live (D11 'won-but-not-live' signal; generous allowances; the homeowner portal I55 makes the customer the enforcement); (3) seasonality (I05).
ideas.trust_note: One number builders understand; unlimited users. Only indirect risk: a tight allowance tempts builders to keep small jobs off JobGuard, which starves the shadow bill — so allowances stay generous.
ideas.regulatory: D09 v2 (tiers, cancellation, price-change notice, grandfathering), D05 bounded renewal authority, D02 VAT. B2B; no FCA. Charging behind G4 (§14.18 enables subscription independently of fees).
ideas.build_dependency: M4-13 subscription terms, M4-14 concurrency metering (must become required), M4-11 Stripe hosted sign-up, M4-16 dunning. Medium (2–4 weeks) once SV-4 lands; month-boundary property tests.
ideas.gaming_risk: Delaying switch-live or locking early to shrink the count is self-harming (no watchdog, no final check) and already a D11 signal. Peak counting on immutable events resists close-and-reopen.
ideas.precedent: ServiceM8 £25/£59/£119 by jobs with unlimited users; report §'UK builders already pay £25–£45' and §Recommendation.
ideas.merged_from: Live-jobs ladder (add-ons lens); Live-job slot meter with soft overage (analogues); Peak-live-jobs bands with Contractor tier (behavioural); Watchdog work allowance — meter verdict (prevention lens)

ideas.name: Soft over-limit: per-slot overage or one-month step, never a block
ideas.mechanism: When peak live jobs exceed the tier, either bill a flat extra slot on the next invoice (illustrative £8–£9 Solo, £7 Builder, £5 Firm per job-month) or bill that month at the next band with a one-job-below warning; both are metered from M4-14 events, cite the jobs, and are pre-approved as a bounded standing authority capped at one tier step; without pre-approval an over-limit raises a Decision and the job still goes live. Slot prices are set so persistent overage ≈ the upgrade step, so the nudge is arithmetic.
ideas.who_pays: Builder, monthly in arrears

revenue_per_year.firm: £0–£320 (only if peaks exceed 25 or a tight top band is chosen)

ideas.assumptions: Solo peaks at a 4th job 2–3 months a year; Small/Firm sit inside their bands. Sources disagree on shape: per-slot (add-ons) vs whole-month step (behavioural); prices illustrative. A fairness device, not a revenue line.
ideas.trust_note: Softer than a hard cliff, but builders prefer flat prices to running meters (Prelec & Loewenstein); overage must be rare and shown as 'cheaper than upgrading this month'.
ideas.regulatory: D09 v2 slot price and cap; D05 bounded authority or a per-overage Decision; D02.
ideas.build_dependency: M4-14 metering, M4-13 terms, M4-10 invoice lines. Low once M4-14 exists.
ideas.gaming_risk: A stale 'live' job must never bill overage: builders need a visible live list with one-tap close (recorded reason) before any charge.
ideas.precedent: ServiceM8 15p per extra job on Premium Plus; YourTradebase £15 per extra user.
ideas.merged_from: Per-live-job overage (add-ons); overage element of Live-job slot meter (analogues); monthly auto-step (behavioural)

ideas.name: Weighted job slots: small jobs count half, very large jobs count double
ideas.mechanism: At switch-live the frozen accepted_net_value (M1-7) fixes a slot weight: ≤£2,500 = 0.5, £2,500–£75k = 1, £75k–£200k = 2, >£200k = 3; the meter compares weighted peak to the allowance. Weight never changes with variations or catches, so nothing JobGuard finds moves the meter.
ideas.who_pays: Builder, via I01/I02 mechanics

revenue_per_year.firm: £0 in-archetype; tail only (ten £150k jobs → Contractor ≈ £2,988 instead of £1,428)

ideas.assumptions: Firm job-value distribution guessed; thresholds illustrative. Disagreement: the analogues source recommends against it as value metering by the back door; the add-ons source sees it as the job-count-preserving way to protect the top of the ladder.
ideas.trust_note: Half-weight for small jobs is plainly pro-builder and pulls small jobs onto JobGuard; the large-job weight is a mild value tilt that must be stated in one sentence and never re-weighted mid-job.
ideas.regulatory: D09 v2 weights and thresholds only.
ideas.build_dependency: M4-14 (weight on the activation event); M1-7 frozen value exists. Low.
ideas.gaming_risk: Splitting a contract into several jobs creates more slots (self-limiting); under-quoting below a threshold is implausible because the accepted quote is the customer's contract.
ideas.precedent: None in trade software; Procore/Buildertrend price on volume (the rejected turnover meter).
ideas.merged_from: Weighted job slots (add-ons lens)

ideas.name: Documents-checked allowance inside the live-jobs tiers
ideas.mechanism: Each tier includes a monthly allowance of checking work — supplier documents through intake (M2-2) plus POs checked (M2-1), e.g. 40 / 150 / 500 — metered from immutable intake events aggregated per period (M4-14 pattern). Over allowance: £0.40 per extra document or a next-period upgrade proposal; never a mid-period block. Statement line reads 'documents checked', never 'money saved'. Fixes the meter's job-size blindness without turnover.
ideas.who_pays: Builder (subscription, D05)

revenue_per_year.firm: £0 at ~150/month; an outlier (3 large jobs, 400 docs/month on Solo) pays ~£150/month and is steered to Firm

ideas.assumptions: ~8/25/50 supplier documents per £8k/£25k/£60k job; £0.40 ≈ 3× marginal extraction cost. Incremental revenue for typical archetypes ≈ £0; it changes which tier atypical builders land on.
ideas.trust_note: Paying for verifiable checking work is the one place a prevention product can charge for effort without claiming an unprovable saving (labour illusion, report §'The hidden final check'). Never framed as a share of savings.
ideas.regulatory: D09 v3 (allowances, overage, notice), D05, D02.
ideas.build_dependency: M4-14 gains a document meter from M2-2 intake events; M4-11/M4-13. Low-medium.
ideas.gaming_risk: Withholding documents to stay under allowance is self-defeating (no checks) and feeds the I07 activity condition; counters must be rebuildable so an inconsistent count cannot charge.
ideas.precedent: Dext prices by document volume; Xero Ignite caps bills/invoices per month.
ideas.merged_from: Watchdog work allowance inside the live-jobs tiers (prevention lens)

ideas.name: Seasonal pause / dormant plan
ideas.mechanism: When the meter reads zero live jobs (or on request), the builder switches to Dormant at £5–£9/month (or £0 under one source) for up to 2–4 months a year: data, quoting and free quote flow stay on, watchdog and locks off, evidence accepted but not analysed; any switch-live ends dormancy at the next period boundary. Paused periods create a £0/nominal D09 period obligation with reason `paused`.
ideas.who_pays: Builder at the reduced rate

revenue_per_year.solo: £5 direct, ~£15 retained (or +£12 vs an annual-discount baseline)

ideas.assumptions: 30% of solos pause 2 months; 12% would otherwise cancel and half never return. Sources differ on price (£0/£5/£9) and on whether the pause replaces the annual discount (behavioural lens says yes). Research calls the winter pause an untested hypothesis.
ideas.trust_note: Matches how building work runs and respects cash-poor sole traders; say in one sentence that jobs closed without a lock get no final check.
ideas.regulatory: D09 (pause terms), D05 (£0 periods, reactivation authority). B2B.
ideas.build_dependency: `paused` state in the subscription period machine (M4-11/M4-13) and M4-14 zero-live rule. Small.
ideas.gaming_risk: Pausing while jobs are effectively live but unswitched — same 'keep jobs off the system' risk, mitigated by generous allowances, not policing.
ideas.precedent: No trade-app pause found; general SaaS pause plans.
ideas.merged_from: Seasonal dormant plan (services); Winter pause instead of two months free (behavioural); pause element of Annual upfront plan (add-ons); pause options in Live-job slot meter (analogues) and Watchdog work allowance (prevention)

ideas.name: Annual prepay plan ('two months free'), offered never forced
ideas.mechanism: Annual prepayment at 10× monthly (£290/£590/£1,190) via one Stripe hosted checkout (M4-11) and one platform invoice; upgrades pro-rated, downgrades at renewal; no deeper introductory discounts. Alternative from the behavioural lens: one month free (8%) or none, using the pause (I05) as the retention device instead.
ideas.who_pays: Builder, once a year in advance

revenue_per_year.solo: £290 (£58 less than monthly, paid day one)

ideas.assumptions: Take-up 15–20% (market norm); churn-reduction claims are confounded by self-selection (report §'Offer annual billing'). Value is cash timing and selection, not margin.
ideas.trust_note: Standard and transparent; the builder chooses.
ideas.regulatory: D09 v2 annual terms/refunds, D05 auto-renew notice, D02 VAT point at invoice date.
ideas.build_dependency: M4-13 billing-cycle basis, M4-11, M4-10. Low.
ideas.gaming_risk: Buying annual Solo then running 8 live jobs — handled by I02/I03.
ideas.precedent: YourTradebase, Powered Now, Joist 'two months free'; Site Samurai 17% annual.
ideas.merged_from: Annual upfront plan (add-ons); Winter pause instead of two months free — annual variant (behavioural)

ideas.name: Value-floor guarantee: documented catches or your subscription back
ideas.mechanism: On Builder and Firm tiers, if the rolling-12-month value receipt (SV-6, posted facts only: supplier corrections, confirmed final-check extras, recovered cash, builder-confirmed prevented findings) totals less than N× the subscription paid, the builder claims a subscription credit for the shortfall up to 100% of that year's subscription, issued as an M4-10 credit note with linked journal. Conditions: minimum documents processed and final accounts locked so JobGuard had the chance to work. Credit applies to subscription only, never to a success fee. Variants: N=3 at current prices; N=5 with Builder £79/Firm £149; N=4 on a watchdog add-on (I08).
ideas.who_pays: Nobody directly; JobGuard bears refund risk and holds market-rate pricing
ideas.assumptions: Uplift = price held £10–£30/month higher than otherwise; claim rate 10–15% × ~50% credit. Sources disagree on multiple (3×/4×/5×) and whether to raise list price. No quantitative SaaS evidence on money-back guarantees exists.
ideas.trust_note: JobGuard bears the risk, the strongest quality signal the research identifies; honest only if 'tracked' is labelled as the builder's own work and 'flagged' is never 'saved' (§14.1). Not insurance.
ideas.regulatory: D09 v3 terms and claim window; D02 credit-note VAT; confirm not a contract of insurance. B2B.
ideas.build_dependency: SV-6 value receipt as a documented-value ledger; M4-10 credit notes; M4-11. Low.
ideas.gaming_risk: Under-using the product to trigger the credit — activity conditions, full year paid first, cap at subscription paid; dismissals never reduce the ledger retroactively.
ideas.precedent: Chargeflow '4x ROI guarantee'; BigChange '£5 per £1' claim (unguaranteed).
ideas.merged_from: Documented-value guarantee (prevention); Value-floor guarantee (behavioural); guarantee element of Watchdog add-on tier (analogues)

ideas.name: Watchdog tier: the prevention engine as the Builder+ differentiator or a priced add-on
ideas.mechanism: Keep the whole job spine (quote, switch-live, Log an extra, proof, final account, invoice, final check) on every tier. Put the merchant-document watchdog — inbound supplier-invoice intake, extraction, three-way matching, overcharge/short-delivery findings, readiness warnings, proof-before-cover prompts, Decision Inbox (M2-1..M2-5) — on Builder and above, or sell it as a per-tier add-on (+£15/+£30/+£60 a month) backed by the I07 guarantee. Structurally no intake on Solo means no detection, never a suppressed finding. Upgrade prompt is evidence-based ('you uploaded 14 supplier invoices this month').
ideas.who_pays: Builder (tier step or add-on)
ideas.assumptions: Solo materials ~£50k/yr make checking worth >£30/month; attach 30–70% (Tradify's bill reader and ApprovalMax matching are paid upsells). Fee-side cost: no intake on Solo means no supplier-document shadow signals or refunds from Solo tenants.
ideas.trust_note: Uncomfortable: it withholds prevention from the cheapest customers and sits near 'JobGuard knew but did not say'; acceptable only because JobGuard genuinely does not hold the document. A tier gate can never suppress a must-surface finding on anything JobGuard actually holds. The add-on-with-guarantee form is the most honest route to charging for prevention (rated 5 by its source).
ideas.regulatory: D09 v2 feature matrix and guarantee terms; D11/D13 must-surface rule unaffected; D02; §14.1 forbidden claims in guarantee wording.
ideas.build_dependency: M2-1..M2-5 built or in flight; per-tier entitlement check in intake (M4-13/M4-14) and a builder-confirmed-finding projection. Low-medium.
ideas.gaming_risk: Solo uploading invoices as 'proof photos' — photos on Solo are evidence only, detector does not run. Loose confirmation only reduces JobGuard's refund exposure.
ideas.precedent: Tradify Lite £34 vs Plus £44 (SmartRead); Powered Now Premium receipts; ApprovalMax Advanced; Chargeflow guarantee.
ideas.merged_from: Watchdog depth as tier differentiator (add-ons); Watchdog add-on tier with ROI guarantee (analogues)

ideas.name: Value-indexed price step at renewal (opt-in tier proposal or capped escalator)
ideas.mechanism: At renewal a worker builds the 12-month value receipt from posted facts. Variant A: if documented value > 8× subscription, propose the next tier showing numbers and what it adds; the builder accepts by an explicit Decision creating a new bounded authority, declining changes nothing. Variant B: terms pre-agree an annual step of the lesser of 8% or a first-digit-preserving amount (£29→£31, £59→£64, £119→£129), applied only when tracked+recovered ≥ 20× subscription, otherwise frozen and the receipt says so; 30 days' notice, cancel without penalty, `subscription_terms` version references the receipt hash.
ideas.who_pays: Builder from year 2
ideas.assumptions: A: acceptance 20–30% × step £30–£80/month. B: 75% qualify. Dual-entitlement research finds cost-justified rises fair and advantage-taking unfair; value-pegged rises are untested.
ideas.trust_note: Reads as 'you did well so we charge more' unless opt-in with real extra capacity (A) or tiny with a visible freeze (B). Never cite JobGuard-found catches as justification — the fee already pays for those.
ideas.regulatory: D09 v3 price-change/notice/grandfathering, D05 (a tier change is a new authority), UCTA reasonableness, D02.
ideas.build_dependency: SV-6 ledger; M4-14 upgrade proposals; `subscription_terms` versioning and an anniversary worker. Small.
ideas.gaming_risk: JobGuard-side temptation to inflate 'documented value' — only confirmed/settled events, same figures shown all year.
ideas.precedent: Usage-cap upgrade prompts (ServiceM8, Xero); 5–10% SaaS uplift clauses; no outcome-indexed precedent.
ideas.merged_from: Value-indexed tier step at renewal (prevention); Value-receipt annual review with conditional escalator (behavioural)

ideas.name: Card at switch-live: first live job subscription-free, fee charged normally
ideas.mechanism: Quoting stays free forever (§5.10). The switch-live screen is the paywall: card captured on Stripe hosted sign-up (M4-11), first live job's subscription waived up to 90 days, success fee applies normally on that job so the builder experiences the real model; the period obligation starts when the waiver ends.
ideas.who_pays: Builders who win a job and switch it live

revenue_per_year.solo: £290 year 1 per convert; expected revenue per free quoter ~£21→~£52 if conversion rises 6%→15%

ideas.assumptions: ChartMogul card-required 25–35% vs no-card 4–6% is B2B SaaS, not tradespeople; whether a card at switch-live helps or hurts is untested (report §'Let the trial run').
ideas.trust_note: Pay when you commit is intuitive and the free first job is a real gift; a sceptic asked for a card before seeing value may bounce — A/B test.
ideas.regulatory: D09 trial terms, D05 bounded renewal authority; §5.10 preserved because the charge arises at switch-live.
ideas.build_dependency: Wire M4-11 sign-up to the switch-live command (M1-7). Small-medium.
ideas.gaming_risk: Leaving the first job live to stretch the window — 90-day cap.
ideas.precedent: ServiceM8 30 free jobs; Qted 3 months free with card; report §Recommendation.
ideas.merged_from: Card at switch-live (behavioural lens)

ideas.name: Multi-entity group account with pooled live-job allowance
ideas.mechanism: Link separate tenants (Ltd + sole-trader CIS entity, sister company, JV) under one owner login with consolidated reporting, a shared rate book and a pooled allowance; each entity keeps full RLS, with one explicitly reviewed read-only cross-tenant reporting path. Parent plan plus £49/month per extra entity; pooled allowance never priced below the sum of the tiers it replaces.
ideas.who_pays: Group owner, monthly
ideas.assumptions: 10% of small firms and 30% of firms (1.5 extra entities) have a second entity.
ideas.trust_note: Straightforward; the cross-tenant read must be a reviewed exception, not a shortcut.
ideas.regulatory: AGENTS §5.1 isolation review; D09 pricing.
ideas.build_dependency: New control-plane task (tenant group, owner linkage, reviewed projection), M4-14 pooled metering, M4-13. Medium with mandatory security review.
ideas.gaming_risk: Entity splitting to reach cheaper tiers — defeated by pooled pricing.
ideas.precedent: Payaca Enterprise 'multi-entity'; Procore volume pricing.
ideas.merged_from: Multi-entity group account (services lens)

ideas.name: Documented supplier correction fee: prevented overcharge proved by the supplier's own credit note or reissued invoice
ideas.mechanism: New category `supplier_overcharge_corrected_pre_payment`: (1) M2-5 raises a cited discrepancy Decision on an unpaid supplier line (price above agreed rate, quantity above GRN, duplicate, pack-unit error); (2) builder resolves it as 'disputing with supplier'; (3) a later supplier credit note/reissued invoice/statement arrives through intake, is human-confirmed and matched to the same supplier, invoice and line; (4) documented reduction ≥ £25 net. Fee variants: greater of 5% and £10 capped £250 per catch; or flat £10 per confirmed correction capped £40/month. Same locking/unique-derivation rules as §14.9; posted as a labelled 'supplier correction' statement line, approved per statement, collected via M4-11/M4-12. If the builder had already paid and cash comes back, the 10% `supplier_overcharge` category applies instead — never both. Wording factual ('line 3 was £180 above your agreed rate; Supplier X issued credit note C567'), never 'saved you'.
ideas.who_pays: Builder, monthly
ideas.assumptions: Materials 35–40% of turnover; documented corrections ≈ 0.75% of materials spend or one per £10k spend; 30% never re-uploaded. No UK data on small-builder supplier error rates exists; large-firm AP audits recover ~0.1% after controls. Adoption (uploading supplier documents at all) is the real driver.
ideas.trust_note: 'JobGuard spotted it, showed the arithmetic, the merchant's own paperwork proves it' is the strongest fairness position for prevention; risks are nickel-and-diming on £10 catches (roll floors into one monthly line) and a taxi-meter feel — offer as an alternative to I08, not stacked on it. Fee is on the documented correction JobGuard flagged first, not on a proven saving.
ideas.regulatory: D03 v3 new category with evidence sufficiency (both documents via intake with hashes/object versions), D01 v4 rate/floor/cap, D02; G4.
ideas.build_dependency: M2-2→M2-5 live and passing the M2-5 held-out gate; a pure predicate leaf; M4-9/M4-10 `documented_correction` source; SV-6 'Corrected before you paid' card. Medium (2–3 weeks).
ideas.gaming_risk: Unrelated discount dressed as a correction — require the Decision to precede the correction, line match and builder confirmation 'corrected as flagged' (D11 signal when corrections exceed flagged deltas). VAT-only reissues count only the flagged line's net delta. JobGuard over-flagging bounded by builder confirmation, supplier document and cap.
ideas.precedent: Chargeflow $29 per deflected chargeback; PRGX/apexanalytix 20–30% post-payment only; ApprovalMax/Planyard sell matching as a tier feature; nobody charges on pre-payment corrections.
ideas.merged_from: Documented supplier correction fee (prevention); Flat per-catch fee on confirmed prevented supplier overcharges (analogues)

ideas.name: Applied supplier credit notes as qualifying recovery (D03 v3)
ideas.mechanism: A credit note raised after the builder paid an overcharged invoice qualifies once shown applied — consumed against a later supplier invoice the builder then paid in full — evidenced by supplier statement or the later invoice carrying the credit line, matched in intake with the 'later invoice paid' fact from M4-7/M4-8. Qualifying principal = applied credit net of VAT; ordinary 10% via the v3 routine with source identity (credit note id, applied invoice id). Only for overcharges JobGuard flagged and the builder opened as a case with terms approved. Unapplied credits and pre-payment reductions never qualify; a reversed credit triggers compensation.
ideas.who_pays: Builder, 10% of applied credit, after the next supplier bill settles
ideas.assumptions: Materials 40% of turnover; post-payment overcharges 0.5% of materials or 2% of invoices; 60–70% settled by credit rather than cash. Honest conclusion: supplier-overcharge fees are small money at any archetype.
ideas.trust_note: Real money the builder had lost; '10% for noticing' friction is answered by requiring a JobGuard-originated flag and an explicit case. Suppliers pay nothing, so the watchdog stays clean.
ideas.regulatory: D03 v3 (the plan says applied credits stay excluded until an approved extension), D01, D02; G4.
ideas.build_dependency: Supplier intake (0033/0036/0037), recovery cases (0034), M4-7/M4-8, supplier statement ingestion via SV-7. Small-medium plus D03 revision.
ideas.gaming_risk: Double counting a credit and a cash refund — unique derivation identity per case line; price cuts relabelled as credits — only credits linked to a flagged overcharge count; require hashed supplier documents, never builder attestation.
ideas.precedent: PRGX/apexanalytix contingency fees include credit memos taken.
ideas.merged_from: Success fee on applied supplier credit notes (behavioural); Applied supplier credit notes as qualifying recovery (analogues)

ideas.name: Statutory late-payment interest and compensation on business customers, claimed inside an opened withheld-payment case
ideas.category: D03 extension — money on top of principal
ideas.mechanism: For business debtors only, the Late Payment of Commercial Debts (Interest) Act 1998 gives base + 8% interest and fixed £40/£70/£100 compensation per invoice. JobGuard computes the exact entitlement from immutable invoice issue/due dates and bank-feed settlement dates (versioned pure function, base rate as a dated fact, never model-derived), includes them as separate lines in the builder-approved demand (M4-5) once the builder has opened a case under the §14.7 entry test, and takes a share only of interest/compensation actually paid and allocated (M4-8). Rate variants: the ordinary 10% (two sources) or 50% of the statutory sums (one source); the 10% on principal stays untouched either way.
ideas.who_pays: Builder, out of sums the business debtor paid on top of principal
ideas.assumptions: B2B share of jobs 10/30/50%; 40–50% paid late; ~60 days at ~12–13%; many builders waive interest to keep relationships; only ~50% of claimed sums get paid. Homeowners are excluded by law, hence Solo ≈ 0.
ideas.trust_note: Money the builder is legally owed and never claims; JobGuard visibly computes and drafts, the builder approves every send, nothing charged unless cash arrives. Offer it, never pressure.
ideas.regulatory: D03 v3 (interest/compensation are not 'net principal' as drafted; VAT on interest), D10 (builder sends), consumer counterparties hard-blocked, M4-5/M4-19 template review; not FCA debt collecting per SRA reading — legal sign-off.
ideas.build_dependency: M4-1/M4-2 case types, M4-5 templates, M4-7/M4-8 allocation to interest lines. Small-medium (1–2 weeks) plus D03.
ideas.gaming_risk: Marking a consumer as a business to add interest — counterparty type as a D06/D11 review signal, never auto-added, ambiguous cases excluded. Dates are server facts.
ideas.precedent: GOV.UK late commercial payments; Chaser adds statutory interest; R&D-tax platforms 5–10% of unclaimed entitlements; 'debtor-pays' agencies (unverified).
ideas.merged_from: Statutory late-payment interest and compensation share (prevention); ...claimed inside a withheld-payment case (fintech); Statutory late-payment interest finder (analogues)

ideas.name: Retention release chase fee: percentage only on overdue retention released after a JobGuard-dated demand
ideas.mechanism: Builder declares retention terms at switch-live or application stage (M4-20 ledger); JobGuard raises a Decision when a release date passes unpaid. If the builder explicitly opens a case with fee terms (mirroring the withheld-payment test: past due, own reminder ignored) and approves JobGuard's drafted release application (M4-5), then 5% (one source) or the ordinary 10% (other source) of retention cash settled after opening and bank-verified/allocated (M4-7/M4-8) is the fee. On-time releases attract nothing.
ideas.who_pays: Builder
ideas.assumptions: Commercial share of turnover 5–10 / 25–30 / 40–50%; retention 5%; ~25% overdue at release (BEIS/Pye Tait: 44% of contractors had unrecovered retention — verify before quoting). Almost entirely Firm-tier revenue. Runway caveat: the Commercial Payments Bill (May 2026) bans retention prospectively with a two-year transition, so ~3–4 years of releases remain.
ideas.trust_note: Retention loss is the trade's most resented leak and the chase is visible dated work; 'I'd have chased it anyway' is answered by case consent and the ignored-reminder test. JobGuard must never delay a reminder to let a case ripen.
ideas.regulatory: D03 v3 category, D10 builder-sends, Construction Act notice mechanics via M4-19 reviewed templates, residential occupiers outside the Act; not FCA debt collecting — confirm.
ideas.gaming_risk: Opening a case on retention that would have been paid anyway — date passed plus reminder ignored required; retention paid outside the app stays non-billable.
ideas.precedent: Payapps/Site Samurai track retention as flat features; UK collectors 8–15% on fresh B2B debt; nobody charges on retention release.
ideas.merged_from: Retention release tracking and chase (prevention); Retention ledger and release watchdog (fintech)

ideas.name: Small-recovery fee uplift: 15% band on the first £1,000 or a £25 minimum per catch (borderline)
ideas.mechanism: D01 v4 variants on the coalesced recovery: (a) fee = 15% of the first £1,000 of qualifying net principal plus 10% above, computed cumulatively and rounded once with §14.9 reversal mechanics, bound to the coalesced work item; (b) fee = max(10% × Q, £25), floor biting under £250, shown as an explicit statement line.
ideas.who_pays: Builder, on small recoveries
ideas.assumptions: Base case: 19/24/33 jobs, 70% locked, paid catch on 25%, average catch 2% of job value; no public data on recoverable value per job.
ideas.trust_note: The founder fixed 10% and the report says keep one rate everywhere; banding mirrors FCA claims-management bands, the sector JobGuard should not resemble; £25 on a £60 catch is 42% and reads as a penalty on small honest recoveries. Listed for completeness, not recommended.
ideas.regulatory: D01 v4, D03, D02; avoid 'claims' language.
ideas.build_dependency: Generalise the v3 routine to banded rates/floors with new fixtures; small, but it reopens a fixed decision.
ideas.gaming_risk: JobGuard-side incentive to avoid coalescing so more recoveries sit in the 15% band — must be structurally prevented (§14.10).
ideas.precedent: FCA CMC bands 15–30%; Cosmo DCA £25–£75 file fee; Chargeflow $29 per deflection.
ideas.merged_from: Size-banded success fee (behavioural); Minimum fee of £25 per confirmed catch (behavioural)

ideas.name: Managed recovery tier: 15% drafted-for-you, 20% with solicitor escalation
ideas.mechanism: On opening a `withheld_customer_payment` case the builder picks a service tier recorded before any pursuit: Self-serve 10%; Managed 15% (a JobGuard credit controller drafts reminders, statements and letter-before-claim from cited case facts and queues each send for the builder's exact approval under D10, builder stays sender); Escalated 20% (adds a panel solicitor's fixed-fee letter of claim, Pre-Action Protocol bundle and MCOL/N1 pack the builder files; disbursements at cost with approval). Fee charged exactly as today on cash settled after opening, allocated per §14.8, posted via the v3 routine keyed by job and rate, so 15/20% is a parameter. Desk: one controller per ~150 open cases.
ideas.who_pays: Builder, out of recovered cash, per case
ideas.assumptions: 1/2/4 withheld cases a year, £1.5k/£4k/£6k recovered, 50–70% choose managed at blended 15–17.5%. Case counts are guesses; no UK data on withheld payments for domestic builders.
ideas.trust_note: Opt-in per case with the rate shown before JobGuard lifts a finger; 15–20% sits inside the 8–15% fresh-debt band and under claims firms; visible work is the fairness condition. If the desk ever contacts the homeowner in JobGuard's name it needs a new D10 and legal review; keep the builder as sender. Say on the case screen that homeowner debts carry no statutory interest to offset the fee.
ideas.regulatory: D10, D03 v2 entry test, D01 versioned 10/15/20 rate table, D05 statement approval; FCA Art 39F appears not to cover services invoices (SRA guidance, legal sign-off); DMCC 2024 and AJA 1970 s.40 for consumer chasing; Pre-Action Protocol for Debt Claims; fixed-fee solicitor avoids DBA Regulations.
ideas.build_dependency: M4-2, M4-5, M4-9/M4-10 behind G4 with D01/D03/D10; new `service_tier` on recovery_case, rate parameter, 'drafter' role with no send authority. One task; the real cost is the desk.
ideas.gaming_risk: Open a Managed case for free chasing labour then settle privately — case-open terms, cap on open managed cases per tier, D11 'recovery discussed then no landing' signal; relabelling ordinary late payment — D03 threshold and refused/ignored precondition.
ideas.precedent: UK collectors 8–15% fresh / 20–35% aged; £25–£75 file fee + 6–10% hybrids; Chaser software plus commission collections.
ideas.merged_from: Managed recovery tier (services lens)

ideas.name: Withheld-payment case file fee (£35 at opening)
ideas.mechanism: When the builder explicitly opens a D03-gated withheld-payment case, charge a flat £35 file fee for assembling the case pack, drafting reviewed letters and tracking; non-refundable, not credited against the 10%, posted to the platform statement under the same Decision that opens the case. Builder/Firm tiers could include two cases a year.
ideas.who_pays: Builder
ideas.assumptions: 1/2/4 cases a year.
ideas.trust_note: Paying to chase your own money stings when the chase fails; acceptable because the builder opts in per case and sees the work.
ideas.regulatory: D01/D03 amendment; not FCA debt collecting for own service invoices — confirm; DMCC drip-pricing bites the builder's homeowner bill, not this fee.
ideas.build_dependency: M4-1 workbench, M4-5, M4-10. Low.
ideas.gaming_risk: Opening a case for the letters then settling outside — fee still earned.
ideas.precedent: UK collection hybrid £25–£75 file fee + 6–10%; Chaser.
ideas.merged_from: Withheld-payment case file fee (prevention lens)

ideas.name: Historic supplier-invoice back-audit (setup fee plus 20–25% of cash refunds, builder-commissioned)
ideas.mechanism: One-off audit of the previous 12 months of supplier invoices from before the builder joined: builder forwards statements and invoices; existing intake/matching plus a human auditor compare them with agreed rates, quotes, delivery notes and duplicates; JobGuard drafts refund requests the builder sends. £295 setup (Builder) / £495 (Firm) plus 20% of cash refunds received; Solo no setup, 25%. Separate D03 category, not the live 10%. Nothing from suppliers.
ideas.who_pays: Builder: setup up front, contingent share after refunds land
ideas.assumptions: Materials 40% of turnover; overcharge/duplicate 0.5–0.75% of spend; 40–50% comes back as cash; take-up 20/30/40%. Overcharge rate is the weakest assumption.
ideas.trust_note: Builder asks for it, money is plainly found by JobGuard's work, 20–25% sits below the 20–30% audit norm; must stay entirely on the builder's side of the counter. Credit notes shown but not charged.
ideas.regulatory: New D03 category version and D01 rate; contract terms; D12 for supplier contact data; not FCA.
ideas.build_dependency: M2 intake/matching (built), M4-2 billability, M4-8 cash-refund evidence, statement authorisation. Medium; mostly audit labour.
ideas.gaming_risk: Builder offsets the refund and reports nothing — setup fee and bank-verified refund evidence (M4-7).
ideas.precedent: AP recovery auditors 20–30% (range 10–40%); Inspired PLC telecoms audits.
ideas.merged_from: Historic supplier-invoice back-audit (services lens)

ideas.name: 'Final Check Only' pay-per-use for non-subscribers
ideas.mechanism: A non-subscriber imports the accepted quote, uploads receipts, supplier invoices, photos, customer messages and the draft final bill, pays £29 per check (Stripe hosted), then declares the account complete, creating the §14.4 lock. The §14.5 final check runs on pre-lock evidence; the reveal shows each candidate with evidence; confirmed catches are invoiced on their own invoice via JobGuard's payment link (separate invoice → §14.8 rule 2) at a 15% non-member rate under exact statement approval. Every check ends with a subscribe prompt (members pay 10% and get the watchdog all job).
ideas.who_pays: Non-subscribing builders: £29 per check plus 15% of settled catches
ideas.assumptions: Half of jobs checked; paid catch on 20% (thinner evidence); priced so subscribing wins above ~12 jobs a year. 15% is a second rate needing D01 v4.
ideas.trust_note: Nothing is withheld mid-job because the job is over; the 10% vs 15% gap must be stated plainly. Late extra bills to homeowners are more dispute-prone.
ideas.regulatory: D12 Article 14 for uploaded customer messages; D13 lock/disclosure rules; D01 v4, D03, D02; hosted Stripe only; post-lock evidence never qualifies.
ideas.build_dependency: Quote import and upload-only intake (0015/0025/0033 exist), SV-3/4/5/6, M4-11 hosted payment. Large; after SV-6 and G4.
ideas.gaming_risk: Highest residual: with no bank feed the builder can take the reveal and bill outside JobGuard; the £29 covers cost, the 15% is upside.
ideas.precedent: FairRate £0.99 per audit (homeowner direction); Chargeflow no-subscription 25%; QuickPrice pay-per-quote.
ideas.merged_from: 'Final Check Only' pay-per-use (behavioural lens)

ideas.name: Prepaid recovery credits (borderline, likely revenue-negative)
ideas.mechanism: Builder buys £250 of success-fee credit for £200, valid 24 months, refundable at face less discount on cancellation; v3 fees settle from the credit first in a fee-prepayment ledger separate from the subscription book (no-offset rule untouched). Statement reads '£1,000 recovered · fee £100 paid from your recovery credit · balance £150'.
ideas.who_pays: Opting-in builders, in advance
ideas.assumptions: 20% discount on base fee revenue £55/£210/£700; 15% breakage. Rationale is decoupling payment pain from the reveal (Prelec & Loewenstein) — theory, not measured on tradespeople.
ideas.trust_note: Prepaying 'to be told what you missed' is an odd purchase and expiring credits irritate; must be refundable. Benefits are cash flow and retention, not price.
ideas.regulatory: Single-purpose prepayment (not e-money/client money) — confirm; refund terms; D01/D05; D02 tax point on receipt.
ideas.build_dependency: Fee-prepayment ledger and settlement order in M4-12; M4-10. Medium.
ideas.gaming_risk: Minimal; refunds bound it.
ideas.precedent: Prepaid SaaS credit packs; flat-rate bias evidence (Lambrecht & Skiera).
ideas.merged_from: Prepaid recovery credits (behavioural lens)

ideas.name: Same-screen fee statement with prompt bounded Direct Debit collection
ideas.mechanism: When qualifying settlement is verified (M4-8), show the statement on the same screen as the customer receipt — '£1,000 received · £900 yours · JobGuard fee £100' — with the evidence trail one tap away; builder approves the exact statement (D05 default) and JobGuard collects by Direct Debit (GoCardless, M4-12) within 7 days. Optional bounded, revocable standing authority (≤10% of the verified receipt, re-checked at execution). JobGuard never touches the customer's money.
ideas.who_pays: Builder, same fee, collected sooner and more reliably
ideas.assumptions: 95% collection with same-screen prompt and DD vs 80% for a separate invoice weeks later — guesses; direction follows Thaler's integration principle and the report's warning that a separate invoice 'would feel like an isolated loss'.
ideas.trust_note: The most builder-friendly way to present a fixed fee; the evidence trail on the same screen legitimises it.
ideas.regulatory: D05 bounded standing authority (AGENTS §5.3), D01, D02, GoCardless mandate rules, D10 for settlement evidence.
ideas.build_dependency: M4-8, M4-9, M4-10, M4-12; UI in SV-6. Small on top.
ideas.gaming_risk: None; builder can revoke and fall back to per-statement approval.
ideas.precedent: Paddle Retain/Chargeflow deduct from flows they hold (JobGuard cannot); Fergus nets card fees at source.
ideas.merged_from: Same-screen fee statement with bounded DD collection (behavioural lens)

ideas.name: Quote-stage catch fee on JobGuard-proposed lines accepted by builder and customer (borderline)
ideas.mechanism: When a site-visit review proposes a scope line the builder did not mention (provenance `model_suggestion`, cited per §5.9), the builder accepts it and the customer accepts that quote with the line priced ≥ £100, charge £5 per line capped £25 per accepted quote, recorded from the immutable scope-item identity and accepted snapshot, charged at switch-live to respect 'free quoting never bills'.
ideas.who_pays: Builder
ideas.assumptions: 19/24/33 quotes at 60% win; 1.5/2/3 accepted proposed lines per won job. Proposal acceptance rate unknown.
ideas.trust_note: Charges on the builder's own work; fairness evidence says builders reject fees where the extra 'was already in their head'; creates an incentive to over-propose and strains §5.10. Recommended only as a counted item in the value receipt and guarantee (I07), not as a charge.
ideas.regulatory: Would need §5.10 wording amended, D01, D02.
ideas.build_dependency: M1 provenance exists; fee leaf on M4-9/M4-10. Low code, high policy cost.
ideas.gaming_risk: JobGuard over-proposes; builders retype lines to strip provenance — both damage the product.
ideas.precedent: Qted bundles an AI upsell generator; Buildbite per-user with self-reported change-order lift.
ideas.merged_from: Quote-stage catch fee (prevention lens)

ideas.name: Commercial add-on: applications for payment, Construction Act notices, stage-payment schedules and retention tracking (flat monthly)
ideas.mechanism: Two layers. Domestic stage payments (Builder/Firm tier): a deposit/first-fix/second-fix/completion schedule on the accepted quote, stage invoices from baseline plus approved variations with the proof-photo gate as trigger.
