Commercial add-on (£29–£39/month, or bundled in Contractor): interim applications and cumulative valuations (M4-18), professionally reviewed payment/pay-less/payee notice templates and a deadline calculator with source and version (M4-19), retention ledger with release-due timers, release-review Decision and release invoice from the final-account lineage (M4-20). Every issue is an exact Decision; nothing auto-sends. One source prices it per job at £39 per live month instead.
ideas.who_pays: Builder (add-on)
ideas.assumptions: £468/yr at 30/60–70% adoption tied to commercial-work share; per-job variant assumes 1/4/10 jobs × 3–5 months at 30–50% attach. Sources disagree on price (£29 vs £39/month vs £39/job-month) and on whether retention is bundled or a £9/month add-on. Weak vendor data (Payapps: 79% of subs almost always paid late).
ideas.trust_note: Plain feature at a plain price, far under Site Samurai's £99–£699; one care point: reminders and notices are subscription features and must never blur into the 10% withheld-payment or retention categories (I14/I15), which need an explicit builder-opened case. A per-job price must not read as the rejected contract-value meter.
ideas.regulatory: D06 (reviewed templates, jurisdiction; currently defers notices/retention/DRC from the pilot), M4-19 professional review, no hard-coded universal Construction Act deadline, residential-occupier exclusion, D02/M4-21 VAT and DRC, §14.3 (stage invoices before lock must not vary with shadow signals).
ideas.build_dependency: M1-12 plus a schedule task (medium); M4-18 → M4-19 → M4-20 → M4-21 (high); D09 add-on terms.
ideas.gaming_risk: None commercial; operational failure is a notice served late — M4-19 queued/accepted/served states.
ideas.precedent: Site Samurai £99–£699 flat; Payapps on request; Construction AI £130+; Tradify Pro progress invoicing.
ideas.merged_from: Applications-for-payment and construction-notices add-on (prevention); Commercial applications-for-payment add-on (fintech); Stage payments and applications with notices (add-ons); Retention tracking and release reminders (add-ons); Stage-payment and retention add-on per feature (behavioural)

ideas.name: CIS module: verification records, deduction statements, CIS-suffered tracking and DRC VAT flags
ideas.mechanism: Subcontractor verification/status records, labour-vs-materials deduction bases, monthly deduction statements and CIS300 return data, reconciliation of net paid against gross subcontractor invoices, plus the mirror 'CIS suffered' view for builders who are themselves subcontractors, reconciled against contractor payment statements; DRC VAT flagged (not automated) until D06 review. Priced £5–£15/month, any tier; JobGuard does not file. Optional flat £30–£50 referral to a partner accountant for sole-trader CIS refund claims (refund firms charge 15–30%).
ideas.who_pays: Builder; accountant partner pays the flat referral
ideas.assumptions: Price £5–£15/month across sources; 50–100% of firms with staff pay subcontractors under CIS; many already do CIS in accounting software, so attach is uncertain.
ideas.trust_note: Pure builder benefit (penalty avoidance); the refund referral must be flat, disclosed and optional — a percentage would look like the refund-firm model builders resent.
ideas.regulatory: D06 excludes CIS/DRC from the pilot; adviser-approved fixtures (M4-22); HMRC agent registration and AML supervision if JobGuard ever files — it stays at records and handoff; D02.
ideas.build_dependency: M4-22 at the end of M4-18→M4-21 chain, or an accounting-connector export (SV-7); M4-7/M4-8 for receipt reconciliation. Medium-high.
ideas.gaming_risk: None.
ideas.precedent: Xero CIS £5/month; Hammr compliance payroll; BuildersAI and Procore exclude CIS.
ideas.merged_from: CIS and reverse-charge VAT handling add-on (fintech); CIS module (add-ons); CIS and site-labour compliance add-on (analogues)

ideas.name: Accounting sync (Xero/QuickBooks) and MTD-ready bookkeeping export
ideas.mechanism: Human-confirmed, idempotent push of customer invoices, credit notes, receipts and confirmed supplier bills (three-way-match status attached) into Xero/QuickBooks via an approved SV-7/M5-1 connector, an export Decision binding target company and source revisions, and a monthly reconciliation pack. For sole traders inside MTD for Income Tax, categorised income/expense records their HMRC-recognised software needs; JobGuard does not file and never claims MTD compatibility. £9–£15/month on Solo (free on annual Solo), in tier on Builder/Firm (one source prices £25 on Firm).
ideas.who_pays: Builder
ideas.assumptions: Solo take-up high because MTD makes it compulsory; Tradify includes sync on all plans so it is table stakes above £59. Value is removed double entry, not a measurable saving.
ideas.trust_note: Pure builder benefit; competitors bundle sync free, so a charge must buy real reconciliation work. Data leaving the EU/UK boundary via Codat/Xero/QuickBooks needs D04 verification.
ideas.regulatory: D04 destinations, D12 (customer data on invoices to a third party), D02 adviser-approved tax-code mappings; G5; no 'MTD-compatible' claim without HMRC recognition.
ideas.build_dependency: M5-1 canonical export, M5-2/M5-3 adapters (after M4-23/G5); M4-13 entitlement. High but highest-demand integration.
ideas.gaming_risk: A 'paid' label imported from Xero never counts as settlement evidence for the 10% (M5-1 rule).
ideas.precedent: Tradify/Powered Now/WorkflowMax bundle sync; Xero £5 CIS add-on; MTD ITSA timeline.
ideas.merged_from: Books-ready accounting sync (services, part 1); Accounting sync via Codat and MTD export (add-ons)

ideas.name: Estimating and drawing takeoff with site-walk coverage diff (£19/month)
ideas.mechanism: Upload drawings/PDF plans; the AI gateway proposes measured quantities with citations to drawing regions (proposals only, never invented quantities); the builder confirms and prices from their own rate book into the free quote. The distinctive part is the coverage diff between site walk-through and drawing ('the drawing shows a soil-stack move you did not mention'), which turns prevention of site-visit omissions — JobGuard's largest unfeeable value — into a flat add-on.
ideas.who_pays: Builder
ideas.assumptions: Take-up guessed; Kreo charges £25–£125 per user for takeoff alone, so £19 per business is under market and can rise after pilot proof.
ideas.trust_note: Fully in the builder's interest; 'quoting is free' must not become 'free unless you have drawings', and the model must never fill a line to look complete.
ideas.regulatory: D04 (drawings via approved AI route), D12 (drawings carry the address), D09.
ideas.build_dependency: New task: extend M1-3/M1-4 with a drawing-extraction prompt suite in packages/ai and a golden set (omission, unsupported additions, citation validity); M1-4 rate book, M0-6 storage. High.
ideas.gaming_risk: None commercial.
ideas.precedent: Kreo £25/£50/£125 per user; Buildertrend Advanced takeoff; Handoff $149–$899.
ideas.merged_from: Estimating and drawing takeoff with coverage diff (add-ons lens)

ideas.name: Supplier / materials price benchmark ('you paid 12% over median'), flat add-on, builder-funded only
ideas.mechanism: With opt-in, pool SKU/alias-normalised net unit prices from human-confirmed supplier invoice lines (M2-3/M2-4) across tenants into anonymised bands by region and 90-day window (k-anonymity ≥10 tenants and ≥30 observations per cell); show 'your price vs JobGuard median and best quartile' at PO pre-commit (M2-1), at invoice match and at rate renewal, plus a periodic materials-price-position report. Findings only: no order changes, no merchant contacted, no tenant-identifiable row leaves the tenant. £10–£15/month (tierable £15/£29/£49); free for contributors on annual plans. In writing: merchants never pay for placement, data, rebates or referrals.
ideas.who_pays: Builder
ideas.assumptions: Adoption 20–60% or 'taken'; needs several hundred contributing tenants per region before cells populate — year-2+ revenue; materials 35% of turnover so 3% better prices ≈ £1.5k Solo / £21k Firm, which a flat £15 under-prices for Firm.
ideas.trust_note: This is the 'selling builders' data' risk in its mildest form: aggregated, opt-in, give-to-get, builder-only. Survivable only with an absolute tested rule that merchants never see anything and aggregation runs in an isolated role like `jobguard_shadow`; any merchant payment would drop it to 1.
ideas.regulatory: New decision record (D14 candidate: data pooling) since M5-6 disables cross-tenant learning; D12/D04; ICO anonymisation standard; CMA information-exchange guidance (purchase-price benchmarks lower risk than selling-price exchange, still needs review); merchant trade-account terms may restrict sharing negotiated prices; reviewed cross-tenant exception under AGENTS §5.1.
ideas.build_dependency: M2-3/M2-4 facts (built), M5-4 supplier identity resolution, an aggregation worker under a separate database role with catalog tests, decision record. Medium.
ideas.gaming_risk: Poisoned inputs — only server-verified supplier documents, trimmed outliers; mis-normalised units — M2-4 conversion/confidence gates what enters the pool.
ideas.precedent: FairRate £0.99 audits against local rates (homeowner-facing); Prolo; P3 cost analysts 50/50 savings share; AP auditors sell this at 20–30%.
ideas.merged_from: Agreed-rate benchmark add-on (prevention); Supplier price benchmark (add-ons); Materials price benchmark add-on (analogues)

ideas.name: 'Are you underpricing?' regional labour/selling-rate benchmark (give-to-get, £15/month)
ideas.mechanism: Opted-in builders contribute human-confirmed rate observations (M1-4 rate_book_observation, only rates confirmed on accepted quotes) to a pool; at quote review JobGuard shows where each rate sits against the anonymised band for the same trade/unit/region over 12 months ('your plastering rate is below the 25th percentile of 140 confirmed rates in the South West'); bands appear only at n ≥ 20 from ≥ 10 tenants; seeded with a licensed published price book, labelled as such, until the pool is large. Free for contributors on annual plans.
ideas.who_pays: Builder
ideas.assumptions: One under-priced £8k job corrected by 5% is £400, so it pays for itself on one job; cold start needs hundreds of tenants per region; price-book licence cost not estimated.
ideas.trust_note: Selling rates are competitively sensitive; a builder must never see JobGuard as a channel that leaks prices to rivals or homeowners. Give-to-get, thresholds and a written promise never to sell rate data to merchants, insurers, lead platforms or homeowners make it acceptable; selling it outward would be a 1.
ideas.regulatory: Same new pooling decision as I28; UK competition law on price-information exchange between competitors needs legal review (aggregated, historical, anonymised with minimum group sizes generally acceptable); D12 (none by design).
ideas.build_dependency: M1-4 observations plus a pooling task shared with I28 (re-cut from M5-6). Medium once the decision exists.
ideas.gaming_risk: Junk rates to pollute the pool — only accepted-quote rates count.
ideas.precedent: FairRate shows demand for rate comparison; no builder-facing benchmark found in UK trade software.
ideas.merged_from: 'Are you underpricing?' regional rate benchmark (add-ons lens)

ideas.name: API access and webhooks (£49/month on Firm; in Contractor)
ideas.mechanism: Scoped, tenant-bound read API (jobs, scope, variations, invoices, receipts, evidence manifests) plus outbox-driven webhooks for job events; write endpoints only for non-commercial fields; every commercial action stays behind the command boundary so a token cannot send, issue or charge. Responses byte-identical with and without shadow signals before lock (§14.3), same RLS context. A free read-only accountant seat exists regardless.
ideas.who_pays: Builder (Firm/Contractor)

revenue_per_year.firm: £147 expected (£588 if taken; one in four firms has someone to use it)

ideas.assumptions: Demand from firms with a bookkeeper/ops person; not a Solo product.
ideas.trust_note: The builder's own data leaving on the builder's instruction; no conflict provided tokens cannot reach shadow tables or commercial commands.
ideas.regulatory: D04/D12 (builder responsible for onward destinations), D09; token scopes and rate limits are security.
ideas.build_dependency: OpenAPI exists (M0); scoped tokens and principal contract (M5-7), webhook adapter on the M0 outbox. Medium.
ideas.gaming_risk: M5-7 conformance must prove tokens cannot broaden finance/order/export authority.
ideas.precedent: Standard SaaS add-on; no UK trade tool found charging for API access.
ideas.merged_from: API access and webhooks (add-ons lens)

ideas.name: Paid finance seat for external bookkeepers and accountants (£15/month)
ideas.mechanism: Site users remain unlimited; a separate 'finance seat' role — read/export of posted facts, invoice and credit-note issue, accounting export, reconciliation view — for an external bookkeeper at £15/month per seat, metered on the subscription; Firm includes one.
ideas.who_pays: Builder per seat
ideas.assumptions: Attach 30/60/50%. Bookkeepers are plausibly the buying channel for solos (MTD), so charging the channel could slow acquisition; conflicts with the free practice view in I61.
ideas.trust_note: Fair on its face, but Xero gives advisers free access to drive adoption; consider free for Solo, paid above.
ideas.regulatory: D09; the role needs its own permission scope and RLS tests (§5.1).
ideas.build_dependency: Role/permission model plus seat metering (M4-14 style). Small-medium.
ideas.gaming_risk: Sharing the owner login — not worth policing.
ideas.precedent: YourTradebase £15 per extra user; Xero free adviser access as counter-precedent.
ideas.merged_from: Paid finance seat for external bookkeepers (behavioural lens)

ideas.name: Customer messaging bundle: SMS/WhatsApp delivery of portal messages, approvals and reminders
ideas.mechanism: Portal messages, approval requests, stage sign-off requests and invoice/payment reminders delivered by SMS or WhatsApp Business through an approved UK/EU-resident provider; replies flow into the job thread (and are therefore evidence under §14.2). Monthly allowance by tier (£5/£10/£20), overage at cost plus margin, metered on provider delivery receipts.
ideas.who_pays: Builder
ideas.assumptions: Adoption 50/70/80%; ~60% margin after provider cost.
ideas.trust_note: Standard and transparent; honest wrinkle: replies through JobGuard become shadow-bill evidence, so disclose it in the D12 v2 onboarding wording and never nudge a builder to move a specific conversation in-thread.
ideas.regulatory: PECR (service messages fine, marketing needs consent), WhatsApp Business terms, D04 provider residency, §5.3 (reminders stay infrastructure messages or go through the command boundary).
ideas.build_dependency: I55 portal thread, SV-7 evidence-observation contract, M0-9 outbox, provider adapter with D04 review. Small.
ideas.gaming_risk: Low; overage metering must be exact and visible.
ideas.precedent: Powered Now AI receptionist £29–£39; Jobber/Joist $29–$49 add-ons; Tradify SMS 10p.
ideas.merged_from: Customer messaging bundle (homeowner lens)

ideas.name: Contract and payment-schedule pack: solicitor-reviewed terms, cancellation notice, staged payments
ideas.mechanism: Every quote can carry a partner-solicitor-reviewed contract pack: plain-English terms, a staged payment schedule aligned to quote stages, a variation clause mirroring Log an extra and customer approval, and the Consumer Contracts Regulations off-premises cancellation notice many builders omit (omission lets a homeowner cancel up to 12 months later). £29/month unlimited (Solo/Builder), £49 (Firm), or £10 per quote; bespoke clause review £295.
ideas.who_pays: Builder, monthly or per quote; bespoke one-off
ideas.assumptions: Take-up 40/50/60%; 20–50% buy a bespoke review.
ideas.trust_note: Obviously in the builder's interest and reduces JobGuard's own contingent base (clearer variation clauses mean more builder-captured extras). Not legal advice from JobGuard; the solicitor partner owns the templates.
ideas.regulatory: CCRs 2013, Consumer Rights Act 2015, Legal Services Act 2007 (template supply is not reserved; advice comes from the partner), D06 and M4-19 reviewed templates; no universal Construction Act regime assumed.
ideas.build_dependency: D06-approved templates attached on the M1 quote send path; M4-19 jurisdiction profiles. Small code; legal drafting is the cost.
ideas.gaming_risk: None.
ideas.precedent: JCT homeowner contracts; FMB free member contracts (unverified); no trade app bundles reviewed terms with cancellation compliance.
ideas.merged_from: Contract and payment-schedule pack (services lens)

ideas.name: Certified evidence pack per pack: anchored, signed, court/ADR/insurer-ready bundle (raw export always free)
ideas.mechanism: In-app viewing and plain export of the builder's evidence stay free (data portability). The paid artefact is the M4-3 deterministic bundle — accepted quote, every variation with approval provenance, hash-verified proof photos with server receive times, supplier documents, messages, invoices, receipts, statement of account, reminder history and a factual chronology — anchored with an RFC-3161 timestamp (M4-4), signed (M5-9), with a standalone verifier, redaction/minimal disclosure, recipient-bound authority and a plain-English integrity statement of what it does and does not prove. Formats: dispute/insurer/handover pack £40–£49; anchored pack with verifier report £99–£149; small-claims pack for an opened withheld-payment case £49/£99; ADR-ready bundle transmitted identically to both parties and a CTSI-approved ADR body £79 (one free on Builder, three on Firm), with a £50 mediation-partner referral when the builder books mediation through JobGuard. Triggered by an explicit 'Export certified pack' command that creates and approves the Decision atomically; charged on the platform statement. Packs generated before lock never include shadow content.
ideas.who_pays: Builder per pack (standard packs in tier on Builder/Firm); mediation partner pays a referral
ideas.assumptions: Packs/disputes per year 1–2 / 2–3 / 3–8; ADR dispute rates 3–6% of jobs; prices illustrative; no UK dispute-rate data for domestic builders.
ideas.trust_note: Show-the-work pricing the fairness research supports, and the builder's own record; failure mode is evidence held hostage or charging at the moment of distress with the free export hidden — keep free export one tap away and charge only for anchoring, narrative, verification and formatting. Never 'tamper-proof' or 'court-ready' as proof of workmanship (§5.7/5.8). A dispute resolved through ADR is fee-free unless a D03-compliant case was already open; per-pack pricing must not read as a per-job platform fee (§5.10) — say so in D09.
ideas.regulatory: D07 retention/WORM before Object Lock (M4-4), D12 (customer personal data, redaction, disclosure is the builder's decision as controller), D04 timestamp provider, D09/D02 platform documents and VAT, D10 (no representation); ADR Regulations 2015; not legal advice or regulated claims management — legal confirmation.
ideas.build_dependency: M4-3 (merged #92), M4-4 anchoring (needs D07), M5-9 signed exports, PDF/ADR renderers, a paid document product on the command boundary via M4-11/M4-10. Low-medium once M4-4 exists.
ideas.gaming_risk: Minimal; a builder omitting unfavourable evidence — the pack is a signed manifest of what was included and says so.
ideas.precedent: Claims consultants £350–£1,200/day to assemble bundles; Lytx analyst-reviewed incident packages; FMB conciliation/TrustMark Ombudsman; RICS/CEDR fee models; no small-trade software sells certified packs.
ideas.merged_from: Certified evidence pack sold per pack (prevention); Verifiable Job Record (add-ons); Court-ready anchored dispute-defence pack (analogues); Fixed-fee court-ready evidence pack for withheld-payment cases (behavioural); Automated narrative pack grade of Dispute and evidence-pack preparation (services); ADR-ready dispute bundle (homeowner); ADR-ready dispute evidence pack with mediation referral (b2b2b)

ideas.name: Human-reviewed dispute pack by a panel QS or claims consultant (fixed fee)
ideas.mechanism: On top of I34, the builder orders a reviewed pack for a named dispute: £395 (under £10k) / £750 (£10k–£50k) where a contracted QS or claims consultant (£350–£800/day, 2–5 hours) checks the chronology, writes a factual summary of what was agreed, done and paid, flags evidence gaps and formats it for FMB conciliation, mediation or small-claims; adjudication-grade £1,500+ structured to the CIC Low Value Disputes procedure. Facts and citations only; anything the builder must assert is marked 'builder to complete'. Hosted Stripe checkout, M4-10 service invoice. Preparers work only from builder-visible data.
ideas.who_pays: Builder, one-off per pack
ideas.assumptions: 0.3/1/2.5 disputes a year; 50–70% buy the reviewed grade at £395–£900 blends. Dispute frequency is a guess.
ideas.trust_note: Visible-effort service on the builder's own evidence — exactly why they captured proof all job. Rule: no pre-lock shadow signal may ever inform a pack, or it becomes a disclosure route (§14.3) and a trust breach.
ideas.regulatory: Legal Services Act 2007 (no conduct of litigation or legal advice; label as factual assembly), D12 minimal disclosure and lawful basis, claims-management regulation does not cover construction payment, D06.
ideas.build_dependency: M4-3 live packs (G4 evidence controls), M4-10, M4-11 one-off checkout, review-order workflow and a scoped external-reviewer role; panel contracts. One to two tasks.
ideas.gaming_risk: Packs used to pressure homeowners over favours done free — factual only, builder states the claimed amount, no generated threats (M4-5 rules).
ideas.precedent: Claims consultants £400–£1,200/day; building mediation £75–£300 per party; RICS low-value adjudication £425; HMCTS small-claims fees £35–£455.
ideas.merged_from: Dispute and evidence-pack preparation, reviewed and adjudication grades (services lens)

ideas.name: Homeowner-paid Sealed Job Record (evidence-pack certificate, £69)
ideas.mechanism: After lock and final payment the portal offers the homeowner a sealed record: accepted quote, customer-approved variations with approval records, proof photos of covered work with server timestamps and hashes, builder-uploaded certificates (Part P, Gas Safe, FENSA), final invoice and payment record, RFC-3161 anchor (M4-4); basic PDF free, paid version adds anchored hashes, 15-year hosted retention, share links for conveyancers/surveyors/insurers and export to a property logbook. Strict subset: nothing from shadow tables, findings, D11 signals, supplier prices or margins. Builder opt-in per job, builder-branded, £39 trade price if gifted; homeowner checkout on JobGuard's own Stripe surface.
ideas.who_pays: Homeowner (£69 + VAT); builder may gift at £39
ideas.assumptions: Uptake 10/20/25% of jobs, rising with job size; no market data.
ideas.trust_note: Builder gains a customer-facing proof asset and fewer 'you never showed me' disputes; risk that builders feel JobGuard is selling to their customer — opt-in, builder-branded, no other upsell at checkout. Any watchdog or shadow leak would turn it into evidence against the builder.
ideas.regulatory: Direct consumer sale: CRA 2015 digital content, CCRs 2013 (14-day cancellation, immediate-supply waiver), consumer VAT presentation (own tax review), UK GDPR controller role for the homeowner account (D12 v2), D07 before promising multi-year retention, M4-4 approval; certificates labelled 'uploaded by builder, not verified by JobGuard'.
ideas.build_dependency: M4-3, SV-4, M1-10, M4-4 (D07), customer-facing renderer, homeowner identity (I55), consumer checkout on the M4-11 adapter. Small-medium after I55 and M4-4.
ideas.gaming_risk: Low; a builder uploading a certificate they cannot issue — labelling.
ideas.precedent: Property logbooks (Chimni, RLBA); Buildbite invoices with proof of work; FMB Building Work Guarantee; no UK product sells a hash-anchored job record to homeowners.
ideas.merged_from: Homeowner-paid Sealed Job Record (homeowner lens)

ideas.name: Insurer-paid claim-time evidence pack ('Send evidence to my insurer')
ideas.mechanism: When a builder faces a liability, damage or customer-dispute claim they tap 'Send evidence to my insurer'; JobGuard delivers the signed, recipient-bound M4-3/M5-9 bundle to the insurer's claims team; the insurer pays JobGuard a per-pack fee (assume £75) because contemporaneous verified evidence shortens handling; the builder pays nothing.
ideas.who_pays: Insurer per pack, builder-initiated
ideas.assumptions: Claim frequency 5/15/40% per business-year; £75 per pack — no UK insurer publishes what it pays. Honest reading: a trust and marketing line ('insurers accept JobGuard packs'), not revenue.
ideas.trust_note: The builder chooses to send their own evidence to their own insurer and pays nothing. The per-policyholder data-feed variant is listed separately under I46 as flagged.
ideas.regulatory: D12 (third-party personal data, Article 14 route; insurer as separate controller), D07 export receipts; no FCA issue for evidence transfer.
ideas.build_dependency: M4-3 (merged), M5-9, per-insurer delivery adapter and M4-10 invoice line. 2–3 weeks per insurer.
ideas.gaming_risk: Low; the pack states integrity/existence only.
ideas.precedent: Procore using platform data for insurance terms; LABC Warranty photographic evidence per plot; no UK insurer paying per pack found.
ideas.merged_from: Insurer-paid claim-time evidence pack, variant A (b2b2b lens)

ideas.name: Homeowner-paid 'check my builder's final account' (the reverse watchdog) — listed to reject
ideas.mechanism: The homeowner pays £9.99 for an independent read of the builder's final account against the agreed quote, approved variations and proof, FairRate-style but with JobGuard's own records.
ideas.who_pays: Homeowner
ideas.assumptions: 20% of jobs at £9.99.
ideas.trust_note: Poisons the watchdog: JobGuard paid by the homeowner to audit the builder using data the builder gave it for their own protection, colliding head-on with the shadow bill. The portal already gives the homeowner free transparency. Recommendation: never.
ideas.regulatory: Consumer sale plus a serious UK GDPR purpose-limitation problem (D12).
ideas.build_dependency: Trivial technically (M1-11 plus M4-3), which is why it needs an explicit 'no' in BUILD_PLAN §11 out-of-scope.
ideas.gaming_risk: Not applicable; the risk is to the business.
ideas.precedent: FairRate £0.99 per trade-invoice audit for homeowners.
ideas.merged_from: Homeowner-paid 'check my builder's final account' (homeowner lens)

ideas.name: Pay-now rails on every invoice: hosted pay-by-bank and card with a capped JobGuard application fee, plus opt-in instant payout
ideas.mechanism: Every deposit, stage and final invoice JobGuard issues carries a hosted link on the builder's own Stripe Connect Standard account (direct charges; Stripe is the regulated institution and settles to the builder) and/or GoCardless/TrueLayer pay-by-bank; bank transfer stays free. JobGuard adds a per-payment application fee, itemised on the platform statement as 'JobGuard payment fee' — proposals range 0.3–0.4% on cards and 0.25%+20p to £0.30 flat on pay-by-bank, capped £6–£15 per payment. The provider settlement event becomes a verified receipt bound to the exact invoice, so §14.8 rule 1 (explicit allocation) applies by construction and M4-7 matching is trivial; the payer pays JobGuard-verified details rather than bank details copied from an email. Optional 'Get it now' instant payout at 1.5% (min £1) against Stripe's 1%, keeping 0.5%; off by default, never on fee collections. Payment-service revenue, never a success fee, never offset.
ideas.who_pays: Builder, deducted by the processor and shown gross and net (surcharging consumers is unlawful); instant payout only when chosen
ideas.assumptions: Link usage 15–60% of invoiced value; 2–5 payments per job; caps bind on large invoices (uncapped Firm would be ~£900–£2,160 but a percentage on £15k transfers when bank transfer is free would be refused); instant-payout opt-in 15–25% of rail volume. Sources overlap; do not sum with other rail ideas.
ideas.trust_note: Builders already pay Fergus 1.6% + 20p; visible, capped, optional. Line not to cross: nudging customers toward the paid rail, or pushing links harder on invoices carrying catches (JobGuard benefits twice — fee and cleaner attribution). Instant payout stays honest only if never default-on and priced before the tap.
ideas.regulatory: Connect Standard/direct charges intended to keep JobGuard outside PSRs 2017 — legal opinion required; Consumer Rights (Payment Surcharges) Regs 2012/2018; AGENTS §3 hosted surfaces only, no funds held, no extra rails before their tasks (needs a 'Discovered later' entry and its own task); D02, D04 provider route, D05, D06; G4.
ideas.build_dependency: M1-12 invoices, M4-11 Stripe adapter patterns (webhooks, idempotency, unknown outcome), M4-15 GoCardless, M4-7/M4-8 receipt allocation, M4-17 reconciliation, builder Connect KYC. Medium (4–6 weeks) after M4-11.
ideas.gaming_risk: Low; keep 'provider cleared' distinct from 'settled' across dispute windows; refunds/chargebacks flow into §14.9 reversals.
ideas.precedent: Fergus 1.6% + 20p; Jobber 2.9% + 30¢ and +1% instant payout; Buildertrend Payments ~2.99%; Stripe Connect application fees; GoCardless Pay by Bank 1% + 20p capped £4.
ideas.merged_from: Payment-rail margin on hosted pay now (prevention); Pay-now links with capped platform fee (fintech); Opt-in instant payout (fintech); Customer payments through JobGuard (add-ons); 'Pay now' on the portal (homeowner); Application fee on customer payments (analogues)

ideas.name: Deposit at acceptance plus stage-payment schedule collected by Direct Debit or variable recurring payment
ideas.mechanism: At quote acceptance JobGuard raises the deposit request from a D06-reviewed template; at switch-live the customer signs one GoCardless Bacs mandate (or a VRP consent when commercial VRP is available); each approved stage becomes a Decision when the builder marks it complete with proof; on approval the collection is submitted with Bacs advance notice and the customer can cancel any single collection. 'Get paid on schedule' add-on £9–£19/month (or in Firm tier) plus £1 per collection above provider cost, billed on the subscription invoice, never deducted from the customer's payment.
ideas.who_pays: Builder; customer pays nothing extra
ideas.assumptions: Adoption 15/40/60%; collections = jobs × payments × adoption.
ideas.trust_note: Predictable cash is what small builders want and the fee is flat and stated; warn that the Direct Debit Guarantee lets a homeowner reclaim a collection via indemnity even after the work, and a timer must never collect without proof-gated builder approval.
ideas.regulatory: GoCardless/TrueLayer are the regulated institutions; Bacs advance-notice rules; commercial VRP availability is a 2026 risk; D05 bounds only JobGuard's own authority; D06 deposit templates.
ideas.build_dependency: M4-15 GoCardless rail and M4-18 staged invoicing; add-on metering under D09. Medium; late M4.
ideas.gaming_risk: Builder-side: collections for stages not complete invite indemnity claims — proof gate and cancel right.
ideas.precedent: GoCardless pricing; Qted Stripe deposits; Buildertrend/Jobber stage payments.
ideas.merged_from: Deposit at acceptance plus stage-payment schedule via DD/VRP (fintech lens)

ideas.name: Single-use virtual purchasing card per purchase order (interchange share)
ideas.mechanism: When a PO is approved at the agreed price, JobGuard issues a single-use virtual commercial card via Stripe Issuing UK on the builder's own connected account, limit = PO gross, locked to merchant categories; the builder's own money funds the Issuing balance (held by Stripe). The authorisation returns exact amount, merchant and time as the 'paid' fact for three-way matching, and an overcharge is declined at the till, so prevention becomes something the builder feels. JobGuard nets ~0.5% of interchange on successful spend.
ideas.who_pays: The merchant's acquirer pays interchange; builder pays nothing extra
ideas.assumptions: Materials 35% of turnover; 30–40% of spend on cards; 0.5% net share is an assumption — Stripe publishes no UK issuing revenue shares.
ideas.trust_note: JobGuard earns when the builder spends, awkward beside 'we cut your waste', and the builder's own money sits with a provider; no relationship with any named merchant, so watchdog independence survives — disclosure must be plain: 'a small card-network fee, nothing from your merchant'.
ideas.regulatory: Stripe is the regulated issuer and holds funds; JobGuard a programme manager — verify any FCA registration; D04 Issuing data residency, D05 (no standing authority), D12; KYB/AML by Stripe.
ideas.build_dependency: New rail on the M4-11 adapter; Issuing task with PO binding and authorisation ingestion into M2 matching. Medium-large; behind G4.
ideas.gaming_risk: Merchant splitting a charge to beat the limit; personal spend (MCC lock, per-PO cards). No fee on a declined overcharge because interchange arises only on successful spend.
ideas.precedent: Stripe Issuing commercial cards (UK); UK commercial interchange ~1–2.5%; Ramp/Brex (US).
ideas.merged_from: Single-use virtual purchasing card per purchase order (fintech lens)

ideas.name: Regulated escrow for stage payments on large domestic jobs, released against JobGuard proof (borderline)
ideas.mechanism: For domestic jobs above ~£25k the builder can offer 'protected stage payments': the homeowner funds each stage into an FCA-authorised escrow (Transpact £2.99 per party up to £10k; TrustMark escrow from £6 per party); JobGuard's stage-complete Decision raises the release request with the proof pack attached and the homeowner releases (or auto-release after N days without a specific evidenced objection); the provider pays the builder. JobGuard earns a referral/integration fee per stage (~£10) or a ~0.3% share of the escrow fee; never holds funds, never initiates payments.
ideas.who_pays: Homeowner and/or builder pay the escrow provider; JobGuard's share comes from the provider
ideas.assumptions: Uptake 5–10% / 8–25% / 10–40% of domestic jobs; 3–5 stages; £10 per stage or 0.3% of escrowed gross. Sources disagree on trust (4 vs 2).
ideas.trust_note: Homeowners love escrow; most builders hate it (cash-flow lag, third-party release, an implication they need policing). Defensible only when the builder chooses it per job to win a nervous customer with mechanical, builder-favourable release rules; tying release to JobGuard's proof gates turns them into a payment gate over the builder — 'verified' must mean hashes and existence, not workmanship. JobGuard must never earn more when release is delayed.
ideas.regulatory: Provider must be an authorised PI/EMI or client-money holder; JobGuard's role must not amount to payment initiation or safeguarding (PSRs 2017/EMRs 2011) — legal review; AGENTS §3 satisfied only if the provider holds funds; CRA/CCRs; D06, D12, D04; new decision record for regulated introductions.
ideas.build_dependency: I55 stage sign-off, M1-10 proof gates, M4-18, M4-3 packs, provider adapter on the M0-9 pattern. Medium plus contract; M5.
ideas.gaming_risk: Vexatious withholding (auto-release rules); pressure for early release (provider rules).
ideas.precedent: TrustMark escrow; Transpact; Checkatrade Pay; Dospay; no trade app bundles proof-gated escrow.
ideas.merged_from: Regulated escrow for stage payments (fintech); Stage-payment escrow with release on proof (homeowner)

ideas.name: Business finance referrals: selective invoice finance on issued business invoices, and working-capital loans from the cash-flow view (flagged)
ideas.mechanism: Variant A: on an issued invoice to a business customer with 14+ day terms (or a locked final account), a builder-initiated 'Get this invoice paid early' sends the invoice, its M4-3 evidence pack and payment history to an FCA-authorised invoice-finance partner (advances 70–85% at 1.5–4% per 30 days); JobGuard receives a disclosed introducer commission (~0.4–0.75% of financed value, or £150 per facility). Variant B: the cash-flow view shows a shortfall and a builder-initiated 'borrow against this' refers to a business lender/broker for a 1–3% commission on the drawn loan. Both off by default, never in the Decision Inbox or a watchdog Finding, never offered on an invoice with an open recovery case; no data leaves until the builder taps.
ideas.who_pays: The lender, out of the fee it charges the builder
ideas.assumptions: B2B invoiced value £15k/£180k/£1m, 5–15% financed at 0.6%; or loan take-up 20–30% × £10k–£75k × 2%. Commission levels are assumptions; Apollo publishes up to 25% of upfront and monthly fees; UK business-lending introducer rates are not published.
ideas.trust_note: A profit watchdog that nudges builders toward debt looks like the opposite of its purpose, the commission is a conflict, and it collides with the withheld-payment fee on the same invoice (JobGuard could earn from finance or from a case). Invoice finance is more defensible (builder-initiated, evidence pack lowers the lender's dispute risk); loans are 'JobGuard sells you loans', the word-of-mouth line the founder fears. If done, opt-in only, commission disclosed, verifier language clear that JobGuard does not certify the debt.
ideas.regulatory: Limited-company borrowing unregulated; sole traders and small partnerships at £25k or less are regulated credit, making the introduction credit broking (RAO art 36A): exclude them, become IAR/AR of the partner (1–3 months) or seek permission (6–12 months); FSMA s.21 promotions; D12 lawful basis for sharing customer data; D04; D10; new decision record; Expert Tooling v Engie on undisclosed commissions.
ideas.build_dependency: M1-12 invoices, M4-3 packs, M4-16 controls, M4-18 cash-flow view; consented handoff and commission reconciliation. Small; legal gating dominates. Pilot referrals only with a decision record and no JobGuard charge.
ideas.gaming_risk: Low; a builder financing a disputed invoice is the lender's underwriting risk. Internal risk: revenue pressure to promote finance over recovery — forbid where a case is open, audit the offer as a commercial send (§5.3).
ideas.precedent: Apollo introducer terms; MarketInvoice construction finance; Chaser + Satago; iwoca/Funding Circle introducer programmes; Small Business Commissioner £11bn late-payment figure.
ideas.merged_from: Early-pay referral on issued business invoices (fintech); Working-capital loan referrals (fintech); Invoice-finance / credit-control partner referral (b2b2b); 'get paid now' on a locked final account variant of Finance referral (analogues)

ideas.name: Homeowner point-of-sale finance ('spread the cost') through an FCA-authorised principal (flagged)
ideas.mechanism: On a free quote for a domestic job the builder can switch on 'spread the cost'; the homeowner sees an interest-bearing option (7.9–14.9% APR) or a builder-subsidised 0% option and applies in the lender's or broker's hosted journey; on payout (portal stage sign-off can serve as satisfaction note) the lender pays the builder directly and pays commission down the chain; JobGuard's share assumed 1–2% of the loan, measured from the principal's payout report reconciled to the invoice receipt (M4-8). The quote total is identical with or without finance; JobGuard never holds funds.
ideas.who_pays: Lender (interest-bearing) or builder (0% subsidy, 8–12% of the loan); homeowner pays interest
ideas.assumptions: 8–10% of domestic jobs financed; loan £5.8k–£25k (unsecured caps limit Firm); JobGuard 1–1.5% net of the broker. UK home-improvement broker commissions are not published.
ideas.trust_note: Builders win bigger jobs and get paid on completion, but JobGuard would earn from a lender on the builder's customer, commission must be disclosed to the homeowner, 0% subsidies tempt quote inflation the quote watchdog cannot police, and the obvious partner model — Kanda, ~700 tradesperson IARs — was restricted by the FCA in February 2026 and entered liquidation in May 2026; a mis-sold loan lands on JobGuard's brand.
ideas.regulatory: Credit broking (RAO art 36A) incl. 'effecting an introduction'; limited permission unavailable for sales in the customer's home so direct authorisation means full permission (6–12 months, Consumer Duty, CONC 3 promotions — any 'from £X/month' line needs an authorised approver, CONC 4.5 commission disclosure sharpened by Johnson v FirstRand 2025); faster route is AR/IAR under an authorised principal (1–3 months) with each introducing builder also covered; s75 with the lender; new decision record; D12.
ideas.build_dependency: After M1-12 acceptance and I39; principal agreement, hosted journey, payout reconciliation. Technically small (2–3 weeks); regulatory setup 6–12 months; M5, behind G4.
ideas.gaming_risk: Quote inflation to fund subsidies; steering customers to finance for commission — JobGuard pays the builder nothing, one quote total, finance uptake logged as a D11 signal.
ideas.precedent: Novuna Retail Finance; Ideal4Finance disclosure; Buildertrend Financing via Nelnet ($3k–$150k); FCA notice on Kanda; FCA credit-broker guide.
ideas.merged_from: Homeowner finance at quote via FCA-authorised principal (fintech); Homeowner finance introductions (homeowner); homeowner project finance variant of Finance referral (analogues)

ideas.name: Per-job insurance-backed guarantee and deposit protection registered from the evidence pack, with introducer commission
ideas.mechanism: At quote acceptance or after the final-account lock the builder can add an optional, clearly priced IBG (workmanship guarantee insured for up to 10 years if the builder ceases trading) plus deposit/stage-payment protection from a partner administrator (QANW, HIES, CWG, FMB Insurance; LABC Warranty/Build-Zone/Protek for structural work). JobGuard passes builder-consented policy inputs (contract value, dates, trade, address, builder identity) and, for structural cover, maps proof photos to the provider's stage checklist as a signed per-plot pack; the locked scope, approved variations and hashed stage photos are the documentation quality insurers price on. Premium ≈ 0.6–2% of contract value (HomePro ~£23–£48 on a £7–8k job), shown as an included or optional invoice line the customer funds, never pre-ticked; the provider issues the policy to the homeowner and pays JobGuard 10–20% of premium; a 'guaranteed job' badge appears on the portal. The line is a distinct invoice kind excluded from net principal so it never inflates Q (§14.9).
ideas.who_pays: Homeowner via the builder's invoice or the builder as a sales tool; the insurer/administrator pays JobGuard commission
ideas.assumptions: Uptake 25–60% / 30–50% / 30–40% of jobs; premium 0.6–1% of job value with a £40 floor; commission 15–20%. Scheme-member contractors normally sell IBGs directly, so JobGuard's cut must come from provider margin, not a mark-up to the homeowner.
ideas.trust_note: Homeowners increasingly demand IBGs (TrustMark), it helps builders win, protects the homeowner from the builder's insolvency not from the builder, and the commission comes from an insurer, not a supplier. Lines not to cross: never imply cover is compulsory, never make proof gates or the final check depend on selling it, and no watchdog, D11 or shadow data ever reaches the insurer — builder-consented, builder-visible facts only.
ideas.regulatory: Insurance distribution (RAO arts 25/39A, IDD): introduce only within the art 72C exclusion or become AR/IAR of the authorised intermediary (1–3 months); Consumer Duty at the provider; IPT 12%; DMCC drip-pricing (optional, priced up front); D02 for the pass-through line; D12 homeowner data; D04; new decision record for partner commissions; no commission in pilot_no_charge.
ideas.build_dependency: M1-6 acceptance, SV-4 lock, M1-12 invoice line type, M4-3 packs, I55 portal, partner API/CSV handoff and bordereau reconciliation; structural variant maps M1-10 proof stages. Small-medium (2–4 weeks); partnerships are the long pole.
ideas.gaming_risk: Policies registered for incomplete work — gate registration on the completion proof pack; hashes prove integrity/existence, underwriting stays with the insurer; an IBG line must never count as a catch or recovered principal.
ideas.precedent: HomePro IBG pricing; QANW; HIES; FMB Build Assure 1–2% of contract value; LABC Warranty stage photos; TrustMark requirements; Checkatrade Guarantee.
ideas.merged_from: Insurance-backed guarantee and deposit protection per job (fintech); Protected-job cover via FCA partner (homeowner); Per-job IBG/warranty at final account (b2b2b); IBG issued from the locked evidence pack (analogues)

ideas.name: Builder's own business insurance introduction: cover check at switch-live, legal-expenses cover, and the flagged evidence-verified discount data feed
ideas.mechanism: Variant A (clean): at switch-live a non-blocking 'cover check' card compares the frozen accepted value against builder-entered public liability / employers' liability / contractors' all-risks limits and expiry; if thin, missing or expiring, the builder taps through with explicit consent to a partner broker (Simply Business, Superscript, FMB Insurance type) or to a contract-dispute/legal-expenses cover partner, with pre-filled trade, turnover band and job mix; the broker pays commission per policy and renewal; JobGuard never advises or compares. Variant B (flagged, 'telematics'): the builder consents to share tenant-level job-integrity metrics (share of jobs with proof-before-cover, signed variations, locked final accounts, dispute-free completions — counts of server-verified evidence only, no customer data) and the insurer funds a 5–20% premium discount and/or pays JobGuard a per-policyholder-year fee.
ideas.who_pays: Broker/insurer pays commission; builder pays the premium (lower under B)
ideas.assumptions: Premiums £150–£500 / £1.5–3.5k / £5–12k; 10% commission (Simply Business affiliate is 10% capped £100) up to 15–25% as an IAR; 25% take rate per year; legal-expenses £250 premium × 20% × 20–40% take-up. The discount itself is unproven for building work — insurers need loss data, so a single-insurer pilot first.
ideas.trust_note: A is in the builder's interest when cover is genuinely thin; becomes an irritant if the card nags or any feature is gated on buying insurance — never gate, never share job evidence under A. B scores 2: it sells a builder-level data feed to an insurer, on the founder's trust-risk list, and a builder who loses a discount because proof compliance dropped will feel surveilled; build B only on a founder decision and pitch it as 'documented jobs', never 'safe builder'.
ideas.regulatory: FCA insurance distribution: introducer exclusion (RAO art 72C, passing contact details/consented facts, no advising or arranging) or IAR status; financial-promotion rules for card wording; D12 consented transfer (insurer as separate controller), D04; new commercial/legal decision record — none of D01–D13 covers partner commissions; B needs its own data-protection and fairness review.
ideas.build_dependency: M1-7 frozen value exists; builder cover-details fields, consented handoff with audit event, commission reconciliation import; B adds a tenant-level integrity-summary export from SV-4/M1-10/M4-3. 1–2 weeks plus broker agreement and FCA structuring (months).
ideas.gaming_risk: Builders cannot game A; JobGuard drifting into advice wording — copy audit. Under B, selective photography lifts a score — report counts only, insurer bears the risk.
ideas.precedent: Procore Risk Advisors; Buildertrend + Assurely; Checkatrade + Superscript; Simply Business affiliate 10%/£100 cap; UK fleet telematics discounts 5–20%; Lytx insurance partners; Coalition Active Insurance; trade-body affinity schemes.
ideas.merged_from: Insurance introducer: cover check at switch-live (b2b2b); Dispute and legal-expenses cover introduction commission (prevention); 'Evidence-verified builder' insurance discount (analogues); per-policyholder data variant B of Insurer-paid claim-time evidence pack (b2b2b)

ideas.name: Credit-control desk add-on (flat monthly, ordinary late payment)
ideas.mechanism: A JobGuard credit controller reviews the builder's aged-debtor list weekly, drafts routine reminders, statements and 'payment due Friday' messages from invoice facts and queues each for one-tap builder approval and send (D10: builder remains sender). Covers exactly the ordinary late payment §14.7 says can never carry a success fee. £39 (Solo) / £49 (Builder) / £99 (Firm) per month ex VAT; one controller per ~80 accounts; the add-on can never open a recovery case — only the builder can.
ideas.who_pays: Builder, monthly alongside the subscription
ideas.assumptions: Take-up 10/35/50%, anchored on LSBS 2024 (51% of no-employee businesses giving credit hit late payment) and Satago/Chaser at £45–£199/month.
ideas.trust_note: Plain labour for money on the loss the builder already knows about; keep it separate from the 10%/15% case path so a routine reminder is never 'converted' into a fee case.
ideas.regulatory: D10 and M4-16 (builder approves exact text and recipient); DMCC 2024 for consumer-facing reminders; not FCA debt collecting on the SRA reading (legal sign-off); D09 add-on entitlement; D05.
ideas.build_dependency: M4-5 templates and approved sends, M4-16 dunning controls, a 'drafter' role, add-on entitlement on subscription_terms (M4-13). About one task; behind G4 for real customers.
ideas.gaming_risk: Low; disputed invoices route to the dispute pack, and the desk refuses to draft beyond what invoice facts show.
ideas.precedent: Chaser £199/month under £4m; Satago £45/£80/£200; bookkeepers at £100–£200/month show builders buy admin labour monthly.
ideas.merged_from: Credit-control desk add-on (services lens)

ideas.name: Legal and claims-professional escalation: fixed-fee steps via an SRA-regulated partner, or a vetted adjudication/claims-consultant panel
ideas.mechanism: Variant A (Garfield-style): inside an opened withheld-payment case the screen offers optional fixed-price steps delivered by an SRA-regulated partner from JobGuard's evidence pack — letter before action, small-claims filing, adjudication referral for commercial customers — with JobGuard earning a 20–30% referral/resale margin per step or a flat £25 pack-preparation fee; the 10% is stated to exclude these costs. Variant B: for commercial/subcontract disputes above ~£10k, a vetted panel of adjudication specialists, claims consultants and construction solicitors; with explicit consent the adjudication-grade pack (I35) is handed over, the member quotes the builder directly, and JobGuard earns a disclosed 12.5% introducer fee on the member's fees — or, the cleaner default, a flat £250 builder-paid 'referral-ready handoff' credited against the pack. JobGuard never takes a share of the sum recovered and never recommends escalation by model.
ideas.who_pays: Builder pays the partner's fixed fees or the flat handoff; the partner pays JobGuard a margin or introducer fee
ideas.assumptions: 1/3/6 cases a year with £30–£50 margin per case; or 0.3/1.5 referrals at £3.5k/£7k consultant fees × 12.5%. Residential-occupier contracts generally fall outside statutory adjudication (unverified).
ideas.trust_note: Fixed, small, builder-chosen steps make the 10% feel earned, but JobGuard paid by the adviser it recommends is the structure builders distrust in R&D-credit boutiques and upsell pressure inside a stressful dispute reads badly; disclose the amount in plain words on the referral screen, prefer the flat builder-paid handoff, keep tone factual (D10), no exclusivity.
ideas.regulatory: Legal Services Act 2007 (partner must be SRA-authorised; JobGuard only prepares evidence and refers); SRA rules on disclosed referral arrangements (banned only in personal injury) — verify; HGCRA 1996 s.106 residential exclusion; D10, D07, D12 audited handoff; not regulated claims management.
ideas.build_dependency: Recovery cases (0034), M4-3/I35 packs, M4-5, partner directory, consent-to-share record, case-cost ledger line. Small (1–2 weeks) after partner agreements.
ideas.gaming_risk: Panel members over-recommending adjudication — vetting, builder rating loop; JobGuard staff steering for fees — cap and publish the fee. JobGuard must not vary the 10% or the shadow bill by whether escalation was bought.
ideas.precedent: Garfield.Law fixed fees (£2 chaser, £7.50 letter, £50 filing; £1.7m settled); Cosmo DCA hybrid; Helix Law no-win-no-fee final-account recovery (unverified); RKA consultants.
ideas.merged_from: Fixed-fee legal escalation ladder (analogues); Adjudication and claims-consultant panel referral (services)

ideas.name: Pre-send quote review by a panel quantity surveyor (prevention sold as a fixed fee)
ideas.mechanism: At 'Send this quote' the builder can add a human review: a freelance panel QS (~£45–£60/hour) reviews the priced, cited proposal for omissions against the walk-through transcript, rates against the rate book and current merchant prices, missing prelims/skips/scaffold/making-good, contingency and payment-stage sanity, and returns labelled suggestions (§5.9: never a silent edit, never invented prices) within one working day. £95 (under £20k) / £195 (£20k–£60k) / £345 (over £60k) ex VAT; ~40–55% margin. Reviewers see the quote and transcript only, never job evidence.
ideas.who_pays: Builder, per reviewed quote, at checkout before send
ideas.assumptions: 30/40/50 quotes a year, 10–15% reviewed. Take-up is a guess; no data on quote omissions.
ideas.trust_note: Obviously in the builder's interest and disclosed at once; anything found at quote stage becomes baseline scope, fee-free forever, so the service reduces JobGuard's shadow-bill base — say so on the sales page. No shadow interplay.
ideas.regulatory: None regulated; reviewer PI cover and reliance terms; D04 if a reviewer works outside the UK/EU boundary.
ideas.build_dependency: M1-3..M1-6 quote flow, M2-1 rate book, a 'review requested' Decision that pauses send, a scoped external-reviewer role with labelled-suggestion writes, hosted checkout (M4-11; manually invoiced pilot service before G4). One to two tasks.
ideas.gaming_risk: Builder blames the reviewer for a later omission — terms state the review is an aid.
ideas.precedent: Freelance QS retainers from £400/month; FairRate £0.99 audits (reverse direction); Qted AI upsell generator.
ideas.merged_from: Pre-send quote review by a panel QS (services lens)

ideas.name: Final-account desk (done-for-you final account and customer invoice, with catches on desk-prepared accounts permanently fee-free)
ideas.mechanism: A desk operator (QS-qualified or trained admin, a delegated member of the builder's tenant with the ordinary builder-visible role) assembles the final account from the frozen baseline plus approved variations, chases outstanding proof and approvals, drafts the customer invoice and walks the builder through review; the builder still performs 'Complete final account' and the invoice-issue Decision. £150 (under £15k) / £350 (£15k–£50k) / £600 (over £50k). Rule that makes it trustworthy: any shadow catch revealed on a desk-prepared account is permanently fee-free (a D13 `desk_prepared` ineligibility reason recorded on the lock).
ideas.who_pays: Builder, one-off per job, invoiced with the subscription
ideas.assumptions: 10/20/20% of 19/24/33 jobs; desk cost 3–8 hours at ~£35/hour, so £150 is near break-even.
ideas.trust_note: With the fee-free rule it reads as honest help; without it, 'your staff built my bill, then your machine found the holes and charged me' is the betrayal pattern the research warns about. Desk staff must never hold the jobguard_shadow role and must be organisationally separate from break-glass access.
ideas.regulatory: D06 (invoice issue stays builder-authorised), D02 VAT on the service, D13 amendment adding `desk_prepared` as permanent ineligibility.
ideas.build_dependency: M1-12 assembly, SV-4 lock, UIWIRE-9 review UX, a delegated-actor role with full audit attribution, D13 flag on the lock. One task plus policy text; ops hire.
ideas.gaming_risk: Using the desk on every job to neutralise the 10% is the intended trade (fixed fee instead of contingent) and priced so JobGuard is indifferent; the lock records whether a desk actor touched the revision.
ideas.precedent: Outsourced QS retainers include 'valuations and final account settlement' from £400/month; no trade-app precedent.
ideas.merged_from: Final-account desk (services lens)

ideas.name: White-glove import of in-flight jobs and onboarding
ideas.mechanism: Self-serve 'adopt a job' (M1-17) stays free; the paid layer is people: an onboarding specialist builds the attested baseline and variation register from the builder's existing quote, emailed variations, POs, WhatsApp photos and messages on a call, plus rate-book and customer import from Tradify/ServiceM8/Xero CSVs. £49 per job, £199 up to five, £750 Firm package (up to 15 jobs, CSV migrations, two-hour setup). Records carry provenance=imported; the builder attests the accepted value. Rule: anything the specialist personally handled is treated as disclosed_before_lock (fee-free) for that job; automated imports stay evidence and the onboarding screen says so in one sentence.
ideas.who_pays: Builder, one-off at sign-up
ideas.assumptions: 2/5 live jobs at sign-up, 50–80% take-up. Steady-state revenue near zero; it matters for cash at acquisition and conversion of larger firms.
ideas.trust_note: Ordinary in this market; the borderline point is that imported messages and photos are evidence under §14.2 — a builder who paid £49 to have JobGuard read their WhatsApp and then paid 10% on what was in it will feel set up, hence the specialist-handled fee-free rule.
ideas.regulatory: M1-17 needs its own decision record before production import; D12 lawful basis and Article 14 route for imported customer messages; D04 for migration tooling; VAT.
ideas.build_dependency: M1-17 (planned, medium), CSV import tooling, fee-ineligibility flag for specialist-handled evidence. Service layer small.
ideas.gaming_risk: Inflated attested baseline changes no fee under v3 but weakens later catches — imported lineage visibly marked; importing a nearly finished job for a free second check is acceptable.
ideas.precedent: Payaca £1,500 onboarding; Buildertrend coaching $500–$2,000; simPRO setup $2k–$10k (third party); Tradify/Fergus free onboarding.
ideas.merged_from: White-glove import of in-flight jobs and onboarding (services lens)

ideas.name: Firm Care: premium support and named account management
ideas.mechanism: For Builder and Firm plans: named account manager, same-day priority phone line, quarterly 30-minute 'profit review' of the firm's own locked-job numbers (quote-to-final variance, overcharge findings, readiness warnings acted on, capture discipline by site lead, aged debt), template/rate-book setup and new-starter walkthroughs. £99/month on Builder, £199 on Firm ex VAT; one CSM per ~60 accounts. Uses builder-visible data and locked jobs only.
ideas.who_pays: Builder business, monthly
ideas.assumptions: Take 15/40%; larger per-user tools charge firms £370–£880/month for software alone.
ideas.trust_note: Standard and welcome, with one hazard: the account manager is who a builder asks 'is there anything else on this job?' — they must be structurally unable to see shadow signals and trained to give the onboarding-terms answer; a single leak makes that signal fee-free and tells the trade JobGuard staff know things they are not saying.
ideas.regulatory: D09 add-on entitlement, D05 recurring authority.
ideas.build_dependency: M4-13 add-on entitlements, M4-10 invoice lines, a distinct support membership with no shadow grants (SV-2). Trivial build; ops hire.
ideas.gaming_risk: None material.
ideas.precedent: Buildertrend ~£2k/year UK support (conflicting sources); Chaser specialist add-on £900–£2,099/month; Fergus free onboarding hour.
ideas.merged_from: Firm Care (services lens)

ideas.name: Site-lead training and JobGuard capture certification
ideas.mechanism: Paid training in capture discipline — walking a job for the proposal, Log an extra vs the diary, proof photos before covering, readiness checks, reading the Decision Inbox: self-paced online course with certificate £49 per person, live remote team session £295 per firm, on-site half-day £750 for up to eight; later via accredited partner trainers keeping 60%. Optional certificate on the member profile. Honest pitch: trained crews log their own extras, which are fee-free, so the course lowers JobGuard's 10% base and raises the builder's billing.
ideas.who_pays: Builder business; online course per person
ideas.assumptions: 20/30/40% buy; CITB short-course grant eligibility unverified.
ideas.trust_note: The strongest trust signal in the list: JobGuard sells the thing that reduces its own contingent income. Say that on the sales page.
ideas.regulatory: None; CITB approval only if grant-funded.
ideas.build_dependency: No code beyond an optional certification record; content and trainer time.
ideas.gaming_risk: None.
ideas.precedent: Buildertrend coaching; Tradify/Fergus free onboarding, so position as crew training, not software training.
ideas.merged_from: Site-lead training and capture certification (services lens)

ideas.name: Annual profit-leak review (fixed-fee human analysis of the firm's own year)
ideas.mechanism: Once a year a JobGuard analyst (QS or commercial manager) works through the firm's builder-visible, locked-job data — quote-versus-final variance by job type, overcharge findings and recoveries, readiness warnings that cost days, proof gaps, extras captured per site lead, invoice-to-cash days, aged debt — and returns a written report with three to five specific changes to rates, stages or crew habits. £295 (Solo) / £750 (Builder) / £1,500 (Firm) for ~3/6/12 analyst hours; labelled an aid, never quantifying 'money JobGuard saved you' beyond settled figures (§14.1).
ideas.who_pays: Builder business, one-off per year
ideas.assumptions: Take 10/25/40%; larger firms already pay £2,500–£8,000 for independent QS cost reviews.
ideas.trust_note: Sells prevention insight for a fixed fee, the honest alternative to a success fee on unprovable savings; an analyst with any view of pre-lock shadow signals would poison it — restrict to locked jobs and the builder role and state that restriction in the report.
ideas.regulatory: None; §14.1 forbidden claims and D11 advisory-only; analyst PI cover.
ideas.build_dependency: M1-16 signals, VALUE-2 cards, M4-3 packs as sources; an export for locked jobs. Minimal code; analyst time.
ideas.gaming_risk: Over-claiming savings in the report — forbidden-claims rule.
ideas.precedent: Cost-reduction consultancies at 50% of savings; QS cost reviews £2,500–£8,000; no trade-app precedent.
ideas.merged_from: Annual profit-leak review (services lens)

ideas.name: Homeowner job portal: approvals, messages and stage sign-off (free; the demand-side engine and the meter's enforcement)
ideas.category: Demand-side foundation, included in the subscription
ideas.mechanism: Builder sends the homeowner a per-job magic link; the portal shows the accepted quote, priced variations awaiting approval (Approve = an authenticated customer approval bound to the variation revision hash, M1-6/D06), a message thread, stage completion with proof photos and 'confirm this stage is done', the final account and invoices. Every message and approval received through JobGuard is evidence under §14.2 and can support a `missed_variation_final_account` catch after lock; portal approvals make confirmed catches far more collectable. No charge to either party. Meter effect: once the homeowner holds a portal link and expects approvals there, the builder cannot keep the job off JobGuard to sit in a cheaper tier without the customer noticing — the customer becomes the live-jobs meter's enforcement, the honest reason a jobs meter can work where turnover would invite under-reporting. Ideas I32, I36, I42, I44, I45, I56–I59 hang off this surface.
ideas.who_pays: Nobody directly; JobGuard earns 10% on qualifying settled catches that exist only because a message/approval came through JobGuard
ideas.assumptions: Portal on 60% of jobs; 20% yield one qualifying catch at 3% of net job value; 70% billed and paid; §14.17 pilot measurement must replace these guesses.
ideas.trust_note: Builders want customer approvals in writing; the uncomfortable part is that customer messages through JobGuard feed the shadow bill, so JobGuard has a fee interest in routing conversation through its portal — onboarding must say so (D12 v2), and the portal must be the builder's channel ('powered by JobGuard'), never presented to the homeowner as JobGuard checking the builder on their behalf.
ideas.regulatory: D06 authenticated customer approval; D12 v2 role and UK GDPR Art 13/14 notice to the homeowner; CCRs 2013 (a remotely approved variation can carry a 14-day cancellation right unless the homeowner expressly requests work to begin — capture that request); D04 for notification providers.
ideas.build_dependency: M1-6, M1-9, M1-10, SV-7 'customer message page', M0-6 AuthProvider extended with a customer principal that is not tenant membership; must pass SV-2/SV-3 (no portal response varies with shadow signals). Medium (3–5 weeks); real homeowners after G1.
ideas.gaming_risk: A builder keeping the homeowner off the portal to avoid creating evidence is fee-free and permitted (§14.2); manufactured 'requests' in the thread produce no fee without builder confirmation and settled cash (Test E).
ideas.precedent: Client portals in Houzz Pro (£85–£275), Buildertrend Essential, Powered Now Premium, TradeFlow (£36 flat); none charges the homeowner.
ideas.merged_from: Homeowner job portal (homeowner lens)

ideas.name: 'JobGuard-checked' builder profile, verifiable quote stamp and quote-request page (flat add-on, no lead fees)
ideas.mechanism: An opt-in public page per builder showing only builder-consented facts computed from locked jobs: jobs completed with a locked final account, share of variations approved by the customer before the work, proof photos per job, invoice-to-payment days, IBG offered, ADR scheme membership, time on JobGuard — values and dates, not just counts, with 'jobs completed in JobGuard' as the visible denominator. Each quote PDF (M1-5 immutable artifact) carries a QR/hash link so the homeowner can confirm it is the exact version issued (never leaking prices without the quote in hand). A 'Request a quote' form captures a structured brief (photos, access, existing services) that lands in Walk it, attacking site-visit omissions. £9/£15/£25 per month by tier or bundled into the middle tier as a hero feature; no score, no ranking, every metric switchable off.
ideas.who_pays: Builder, flat monthly
ideas.assumptions: Adoption 40–50%; value depends on JobGuard becoming recognisable to homeowners, so early on it may work better bundled. Benchmarks: Checkatrade £30/month, Which? Trusted Traders from £48.
ideas.trust_note: Builder-controlled, positive, verifiable facts are in the builder's interest; drops to 2 the moment it shows anything JobGuard learned as watchdog (catches, overcharges, D11 signals, dispute counts) because JobGuard would publicly rate its own customer from data collected for them. No leads sold, no marketplace.
ideas.regulatory: DMCC 2024/CPUT ('checked' defined, true, no endorsement of workmanship implied), ASA/CAP, UK GDPR (aggregate facts, no customer data), PECR not engaged.
ideas.build_dependency: M1-5 quote hash, SV-4, M1-10, M4-3, a public read-only route with tenant opt-in, Walk-it intake adapter (M1-2). Small-medium (2–4 weeks); meaningful after the pilot produces locked jobs.
ideas.gaming_risk: Locking trivial jobs to inflate counts — show values and dates; locked facts cannot be edited; count only server-verified evidence.
ideas.precedent: Checkatrade Approved £30 / Growth £59+; Which? Trusted Traders; TrustMark fees; Powered Now certificates; Checkatrade free quoting tool.
ideas.merged_from: 'JobGuard-checked' builder profile, quote stamp and quote-request page (homeowner); 'JobGuard Verified' public profile (analogues)

ideas.name: Homeowner aftercare record with exclusive repeat-work and referral routing to the same builder
ideas.mechanism: After completion the homeowner keeps a free JobGuard home account: job records, guarantee expiry dates, certificates, 'what's behind the wall' photos and reminders. 'Book [Builder] again' and 'Recommend [Builder]' create an enquiry that lands in that builder's Walk it and nobody else's; JobGuard never routes the homeowner elsewhere. Builder pays £8/£12/£20 per month by tier; no per-lead fee on their own customers.
ideas.who_pays: Builder; homeowner free
ideas.assumptions: Adoption 50–60%; one referral that becomes an £8k job is worth far more than the fee.
ideas.trust_note: Obviously in the builder's interest while exclusivity is absolute; flips to a 1 if JobGuard ever markets other builders, insurers, energy or solar to these homeowners — that is selling the builder's customers. Make exclusivity a contractual promise, not a setting.
ideas.regulatory: UK GDPR controller role for homeowner accounts (D12 v2); PECR consent for reminders/referral prompts; the builder remains controller of their customer list; D07 retention for homeowner records.
ideas.build_dependency: I55 portal, consumer identity in the AuthProvider (M0-6) that is not tenant membership, Walk-it intake adapter. Medium (4–6 weeks); after G1.
ideas.gaming_risk: Only JobGuard's own temptation to monetise the homeowner base.
ideas.precedent: Houzz Pro client portal; Buildertrend warranty module; property logbooks; no UK trade app sells exclusive own-customer routing.
ideas.merged_from: Homeowner aftercare record with exclusive routing (homeowner lens)

ideas.name: Verified-builder marketplace: homeowner job requests matched to JobGuard builders, paid per won job (flagged)
ideas.mechanism: Homeowners post a job on JobGuard's public site; JobGuard matches builders with profiles (I56) in range; builders quote through Walk it. Success-only charge of 2% of accepted net quote value, triggered only when acceptance (M1-6) and switch-live (M1-7) are recorded in JobGuard; alternative per-shortlist £15–£50 like MyBuilder.
ideas.who_pays: Builder
ideas.assumptions: 2/3/2 marketplace-won jobs a year at £8k/£25k/£60k × 2%; ignores the large homeowner marketing spend needed to create demand.
ideas.trust_note: The biggest demand-side number, flagged plainly: JobGuard would be the builder's watchdog and its lead seller, the most resented model in the trade; it gains from routing homeowners to builders who run more live jobs and produce more catches while calling them 'checked'; it must never use one builder's homeowners as demand for others; keeping 'checked' credible means policing builders, putting JobGuard against its own customers. Recommendation: do the free directory (I56) and leave lead fees to Checkatrade.
ideas.regulatory: Not a regulated activity; DMCC 2024 paid-placement disclosure and fake-review rules; UK GDPR/PECR for homeowner marketing (JobGuard as controller for leads, D12 extension); consumer law on 'checked' promises.
ideas.build_dependency: I56 profiles, homeowner accounts and posting UX, matching, attribution bound to acceptance and switch-live, M4-10 billing line. Large (2–3 months) plus marketing; M5 at the earliest.
ideas.gaming_risk: High: builders taking the homeowner off-platform to avoid the 2% (Checkatrade's leakage), and the temptation to police that with D11-style signals would turn the watchdog on the builder.
ideas.precedent: Checkatrade £30–£59+/month plus lead pricing (£5–£40 equivalents); MyBuilder shortlist fees £5–£35, £50+ on large jobs.
ideas.merged_from: Verified-builder marketplace (homeowner lens)

ideas.name: Independent completion inspection booked through the portal (homeowner-paid, referral fee)
ideas.mechanism: At practical completion the builder can enable an 'independent completion check': the homeowner books a snagging inspector from a JobGuard-vetted panel; the inspector receives the proof-photo record and agreed scope so the check is against what was agreed, not a wish-list; the report goes to both parties and, if clean, the homeowner signs off the final stage, triggering the final invoice. JobGuard takes a 15% referral fee from the inspector (~£350 inspection).
ideas.who_pays: Homeowner pays the inspector; inspector pays JobGuard
ideas.assumptions: Uptake 5/8/10% (larger jobs); referral rate assumed.
ideas.trust_note: Feels adversarial (an inspector booked through the builder's own tool to find fault), so builder-enabled per job and never offered by JobGuard unprompted; builder-side value is real — a clean report closes the job, releases final payment, pre-empts withheld-payment disputes, and giving the inspector the agreed scope protects against snag-list scope creep.
ideas.regulatory: Snagging inspectors unregulated (RICS/RPSA membership as panel criterion); referral fee disclosed to the homeowner (DMCC/CPUT hidden-commission concerns); D12 for sharing job data.
ideas.build_dependency: I55 portal, M1-10 proof and stage gates, panel/referral adapter. Small (~2 weeks) plus panel recruitment; after G1.
ideas.gaming_risk: Low; JobGuard must not favour inspectors who produce clean reports.
ideas.precedent: UK snagging market £300–£600 (not looked up); Checkatrade Guarantee independent assessment step; no trade app offers it.
ideas.merged_from: Independent completion inspection referral (homeowner lens)

ideas.name: Trade-body endorsed plan (FMB / NFB) with referral fee to the body
ideas.mechanism: JobGuard joins the FMB Associate directory / NFB Strategic Partners as a member benefit; members redeem a verified membership number at Stripe subscription sign-up (M4-11) for 'two months free' on the annual plan; JobGuard pays the body ~15% of first-year subscription per converted member on a self-billed quarterly statement plus a flat listing fee; optional 'Master Builder / NFB member' mark on the customer-facing final account and evidence pack. Success fee unchanged and never shared with the body.
ideas.who_pays: Builder pays the discounted subscription; JobGuard pays the body

revenue_per_year.solo: £247 net year 1, £348 after (no incremental revenue; a CAC/trust channel)

ideas.assumptions: 15% referral is an assumption (bodies publish no partner terms; Simply Business pays affiliates 10% capped £100; Xero 30%). FMB members run a few long domestic jobs, so the live-jobs meter fits this channel better than jobs-per-month would — say so at sign-up.
ideas.trust_note: A discount via a body builders already trust and a mark that helps them win work; refuse contractually any demand for a share of success fees or visibility of findings; the mark must not imply the body verified the work.
ideas.regulatory: Trade-body endorsement rules and ASA/CAP for co-branded claims; none specific.
ideas.build_dependency: M4-11 and M4-13; partner-attribution table, membership-number validation, partner payout statements via M4-10; D09 v2 promo/annual terms. 1–2 weeks after M4-11.
ideas.gaming_risk: Shared or lapsed membership numbers — validate against the body's list at sign-up and annually; one redemption per number.
ideas.precedent: FMB member benefits and supplier directory; NFB Strategic Partners; Checkatrade bundling QuickBooks at 75% off.
ideas.merged_from: Trade-body endorsed plan (b2b2b lens)

ideas.name: Accountant and bookkeeper channel: recurring revenue share, free practice view, and a practice-paid year-end job pack
ideas.mechanism: Practices enrol as JobGuard Advisers with a free read-only practice seat over consenting builder clients (per-job WIP = accepted baseline + approved variations − invoiced, unbilled approved variations, retentions, CIS deductions, DRC flags, locked final accounts as year-end evidence); JobGuard pays the practice 20% of referred subscription revenue for 24 months on a self-billed quarterly statement (success fees never shared). Vetted bookkeepers can also be listed in-app for builders to hire at their own price — with a disclosed 10% first-year introducer fee to JobGuard, or, cleaner, no fee and a free listing. Optional practice-paid add-on: £4 per builder client per month (10-client minimum, £8 on multi-job tiers) for a year-end pack — WIP and revenue-recognition schedule from immutable quotes/variations/invoices (labelled a projection, not accounting advice), unbilled-approved-variations list (all builder capture, fee-free), retention and CIS reconciliations, DRC flags, signed exports of every locked final account; the builder pays nothing extra.
ideas.who_pays: Builder pays the subscription; JobGuard pays the practice a share; the practice pays for the year-end pack; a listed bookkeeper may pay a disclosed introducer fee

revenue_per_year.solo: £278 net (£348 × 0.8) for two years then £348, plus £48 practice pack where enrolled, plus ~£12 introducer

ideas.assumptions: 20% for 24 months sits between Xero's 30% refer-a-friend and its £50 flat referral; effective CAC £70–£286 a year for two years; pack price anchored below Dext's ~$17.70/client; 20–30% of builders' practices enrol at maturity. Only 29% of no-employee construction businesses use software, so the accountant often chooses it; MTD ITSA (April 2026, £50k → £30k 2027 → £20k 2028) is the opening. Direction of money differs between sources (JobGuard pays the practice vs the practice pays JobGuard).
ideas.trust_note: Builders trust their accountant more than any app vendor; ICAEW/ACCA/AAT require commission disclosure, so make the share visible in the builder's terms. The bookkeeper introducer fee is the borderline part (JobGuard paid by a party it recommends) — disclose the amount or drop it; keep the free data-portability export intact so the pack is a convenience, not a toll.
ideas.regulatory: D12 (practice as consented recipient, likely independent controller); accountants' professional commission-disclosure rules; self-billing VAT for payouts; D02 for VAT labels in the pack; 'revenue recognition' labelled as projection.
ideas.build_dependency: M0-6 scoped 'adviser' role; attribution and payout statements shared with I60; reporting layer over M1-11, M1-9, M4-20, M4-22; pack needs M5-1 canonical export and M5-9 signed exports; M5-2/M5-3 make it stickier. 2–4 weeks for attribution and a basic view.
ideas.gaming_risk: Enrolling clients who never use JobGuard — pay share only on collected revenue, stop on cancellation.
ideas.precedent: Xero partner programme (30% refer-a-friend / £50); Dext practice pricing with 10-client minimum; Xero job costing only on its £70 plan; sole-trader bookkeeping £100–£200/month.
ideas.merged_from: Accountant and bookkeeper referral channel (b2b2b); Practice-paid 'year-end job pack' (b2b2b); bookkeeper partner programme half of Books-ready accounting sync (services)

ideas.name: Main contractor / housebuilder / property manager pays per project; subcontractors get JobGuard free (Payapps model)
